translations.literal: Zhongyan was firm within and gentle without; by nature he was extremely filial. Because when his mother was alive they were poor, afterward though he became honored, unless there were guests he did not serve a second helping of meat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was resolute at heart yet mild in manner, and profoundly filial by nature. His mother had lived in poverty, and even after he rose to high rank he would not set out a second dish of meat unless he had guests.

sentences.zh: 妻子衣食，僅能自充。

translations.literal: His wife and children's clothing and food barely sufficed for their own needs.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and children had barely enough food and clothing to get by.

sentences.zh: 而好施予，置義莊里中，以贍族人。

translations.literal: Yet he loved to give generously; he established a charity estate in the village to support his clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he delighted in giving, and established a charity estate in his home village to support members of his clan.

sentences.zh: 泛愛樂善，士多出其門下，雖里巷之人，皆能道其名字。

translations.literal: He loved widely and delighted in good deeds; many scholars came from his gate, and even people in the alleys could recite his name.
translations.idiomatic: Broad in his benevolence and eager to promote the good, he drew many scholars from his household, and even common townsfolk could speak his name.

sentences.zh: 死之日，四方聞者，皆為歎息。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, all who heard of it throughout the four directions sighed in sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, people far and wide who heard the news all sighed in grief.

sentences.zh: 為政尚忠厚，所至有恩，邠、慶二州之民與屬羌，皆畫像立生祠事之。

translations.literal: In governing he valued loyalty and kindness; wherever he went he showed favor. The people of Bin and Qing prefectures and the subordinate Tangut tribes all painted his portrait and erected living shrines to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he prized sincerity and kindness and left a legacy of grace wherever he served. The people of Bin and Qing, together with the Tangut tribes under his jurisdiction, painted his likeness and built living shrines in his honor.

sentences.zh: 及其卒也，羌酋數百人，哭之如父，齋三日而去。

translations.literal: When he died, several hundred Tangut chieftains wept for him as for a father, observed a fast for three days, and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: At his death several hundred Tangut chieftains mourned him as they would a father, kept three days of abstinence, and only then took their leave.

sentences.zh: 四子：純祐、純仁、純禮、純粹。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Chunyou, Chunren, Chunli, and Chuncui.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Chunyou, Chunren, Chunli, and Chuncui.

sentences.zh: 子 純祐

translations.literal: Son: Chunyou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunyou.

sentences.zh: 純祐，字天成，性英悟自得，尚節行。

translations.literal: Chunyou, courtesy name Tiancheng, was by nature brilliant and self-possessed, and valued integrity and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou, styled Tiancheng, was naturally quick and self-assured, and held fast to integrity in his conduct.

sentences.zh: 方十歲，能讀諸書；

translations.literal: At just ten years of age he could read the various classics.
translations.idiomatic: By the age of ten he could read the full range of canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 為文章，籍籍有稱。

translations.literal: In composing essays he was widely praised.
translations.idiomatic: His essays won wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 父仲淹守蘇州，首建郡學，聘胡瑗為師。

translations.literal: When his father Zhongyan served as Prefect of Suzhou, he was the first to establish the prefectural school and engaged Hu Yuan as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Zhongyan governed Suzhou, he founded the prefectural school—the first of its kind—and engaged Hu Yuan as its master.

sentences.zh: 瑗立學規良密，生徒數百，多不率教，仲淹患之。

translations.literal: Yuan established school regulations of great strictness; the students numbered in the hundreds, and many did not follow the teachings, which Zhongyan found troubling.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yuan drew up rigorous school rules, but of the several hundred students many refused to obey them, to Zhongyan's dismay.

sentences.zh: 純祐尚未冠，輒白入學，齒諸生之末，盡行其規，諸生隨之，遂不敢犯。

translations.literal: Chunyou had not yet come of age, yet he volunteered to enter the school, took his place among the students at the end of the line, fully observed the regulations, and the other students followed suit, so that none dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou was still under age, yet he asked to enroll, took the lowest place among the students, and obeyed every rule to the letter. The others followed his example, and from then on none dared break the regulations.

sentences.zh: 自是蘇學為諸郡倡。

translations.literal: From this the Suzhou school became the model for all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Suzhou school became the standard for prefectural education throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 寶元中，西夏叛，仲淹連官關陝，皆將兵。

translations.literal: In the Baoyuan era the Western Xia rebelled; Zhongyan held successive posts in the Guan-Shaan region, in each case commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoyuan period, when the Western Xia rose in rebellion, Zhongyan held a series of posts along the Guan-Shaan frontier, each time with command of troops.

sentences.zh: 純祐與將卒錯處，鉤深擿隱，得其才否。

translations.literal: Chunyou mixed with the officers and soldiers, probing deeply and unearthing what was hidden, and thus learned who had talent and who did not.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou lived among the officers and rank and file, questioning them closely and drawing out what they kept hidden, until he knew exactly who had ability and who lacked it.

sentences.zh: 由是仲淹任人無失，而屢有功。

translations.literal: Because of this Zhongyan made no mistakes in appointing men, and repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to this, Zhongyan never misjudged the men he appointed and won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 仲淹帥環慶，議城馬鋪砦，砦逼夏境，夏懼扼其沖，侵撓其役。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan commanded the Huan-Qing circuit, he proposed building Mapu Fort; the fort pressed against the Xia border, and the Xia, fearing that their route would be choked off, harassed the construction work.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongyan was military commissioner of Huan-Qing, he proposed building Mapu Fort. The site lay hard against the Xia frontier; fearing their supply line would be cut, the Xia repeatedly raided the builders.

sentences.zh: 純祐率兵馳據其地，夏眾大至，且戰且役，數日而成，一路恃之以安。

translations.literal: Chunyou led troops in a rush to occupy the ground; a large Xia force arrived, and they fought even as they worked; within several days the fort was complete, and the whole circuit relied on it for security.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou raced ahead with troops to seize the site. A large Xia army arrived, but he fought while building, and within days the fort was finished. The entire circuit thereafter depended on it for its safety.

sentences.zh: 純祐事父母孝，未嘗違左右，不應科第。

translations.literal: Chunyou served his parents with filial devotion, never leaving their side, and did not sit for the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou was devoted to his parents and never strayed from their side; he declined to pursue the examination route to office.

sentences.zh: 及仲淹以讒罷，純祐不得已，蔭守將作監主簿，又為司竹監，以非所好，即解去。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan was dismissed because of slander, Chunyou had no choice but to accept inherited appointment as Recorder of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and later served as Commissioner of the Bamboo Plantations Office; because these were not to his liking, he immediately resigned.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongyan fell victim to slander and lost office, Chunyou reluctantly accepted a yin privilege appointment as recorder at the Directorate of Palace Buildings, and later served as commissioner of the Bamboo Plantations Office. Finding neither post to his taste, he resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 從仲淹之鄧，得疾昏廢，臥許昌。

translations.literal: He followed Zhongyan to Deng, fell ill and was reduced to incapacity, and lay bedridden at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Zhongyan to Deng, then fell gravely ill and was left incapacitated, confined to his bed at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 富弼守淮西，過省之，猶能感慨道忠義，問弼之來公耶私耶，弼曰「公」。

translations.literal: Fu Bi, governing Huai-Xi, passed by to visit him; he was still able to speak with feeling about loyalty and righteousness, and asked whether Bi's visit was on public business or private business. Bi said, "Public."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi, then governing the Huai-Xi region, stopped to see him on his way through. Chunyou could still speak passionately of loyalty and duty, and asked whether the visit was official or personal. Fu Bi answered, "Official."

sentences.zh: 純祐曰「公則可」。

translations.literal: Chunyou said, "If it is public, then it is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Chunyou replied, "If it is official business, then very well."

sentences.zh: 凡病十九年卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: In all he was ill for nineteen years before he died, at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: His illness lasted nineteen years in all; he died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子正臣，守太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: His son Zhengchen held the post of Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengchen served as a sacrificial officer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 子 純禮

translations.literal: Son: Chunli.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chunli.

sentences.zh: 純禮，字彝叟，以父仲淹蔭，為秘書省正字，簽書河南府判官，知陵台令兼永安縣。

translations.literal: Chunli, courtesy name Yisou, through his father Zhongyan's yin privilege became Proofreader of the Secretariat, signed as Judicial Commissioner of Henan Prefecture, and served as Magistrate of Lingtai and concurrently of Yong'an County.
translations.idiomatic: Chunli, styled Yisou, entered office through his father Zhongyan's yin privilege as a secretariat proofreader, signed as judicial commissioner of Henan Prefecture, and governed Lingtai while concurrently administering Yong'an County.

sentences.zh: 永昭陵建，京西轉運使配木石磚甓及工徒於一路，獨永安不受令。

translations.literal: When the Yongzhao Mausoleum was under construction, the Jingxi Transport Commissioner apportioned timber, stone, bricks, tiles, and laborers across the circuit; Yong'an alone refused to accept the order.
translations.idiomatic: During construction of the Yongzhao Mausoleum, the Jingxi transport commissioner levied timber, stone, brick, tile, and labor from every county in the circuit. Yong'an alone declined to comply.

sentences.zh: 使者以白陵使韓琦，琦曰：「范純禮豈不知此？

translations.literal: The envoy reported this to the mausoleum commissioner Han Qi, who said: "How could Fan Chunli not know this?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported the matter to the mausoleum commissioner Han Qi, who said, "Fan Chunli must surely understand the situation.

sentences.zh: 將必有說。」

translations.literal: He must have a reason."
translations.idiomatic: He must have his reasons.

sentences.zh: 他日，眾質之，純禮曰：「陵寢皆在邑境，歲時繕治無虛日，今乃與百縣均賦，曷若置此，使之奉常時用乎。」

translations.literal: Another day the others questioned him, and Chunli said: "The imperial tombs all lie within the county's territory; repairs are carried out year-round without a day's rest. To levy this county equally with a hundred others—would it not be better to set this burden aside and let the funds serve the tombs' routine upkeep?"
translations.idiomatic: Some days later the others pressed him for an explanation. Chunli said, "The imperial tombs all fall within my county's jurisdiction, and we maintain them without a day's interruption. To impose the same levy as on a hundred other counties—would it not be better to exempt us so those funds can meet the tombs' everyday needs?"

sentences.zh: 琦是其對。

translations.literal: Qi approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi accepted his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 還朝，用為三司鹽鐵判官，以比部員外郎出知遂州。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed Salt and Iron Judge of the Three Departments; as Outer Bureau Vice Director he went out to govern Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to court he was made salt and iron judge of the Three Departments, then left the capital as outer bureau vice director to govern Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 滬南有邊事，調度苛棘，純禮一以靜待之，辨其可具者，不取於民。

translations.literal: On the Lunan frontier there were border affairs; the requisitions were harsh and exacting. Chunli met them all with calm, distinguished what could be supplied, and took nothing from the people.
translations.idiomatic: When border troubles arose on the Lunan frontier, the requisitions were severe and burdensome. Chunli responded with steady calm, determined what could legitimately be furnished, and levied nothing beyond that on the populace.

sentences.zh: 民圖像於廬，而奉之如神，名曰「范公庵」。

translations.literal: The people painted his portrait in a hut and honored him as a god, naming it the "Hermitage of Lord Fan."
translations.idiomatic: The people painted his likeness in a roadside shrine and venerated it as divine, calling the place the Hermitage of Lord Fan.

sentences.zh: 草場火，民情疑怖，守吏惕息俟誅。

translations.literal: A hay storage yard caught fire; the people were suspicious and frightened, and the guarding officials trembled in fear awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: When a hay storage yard caught fire, the people grew fearful and suspicious, and the officials in charge trembled, expecting to be punished with death.

sentences.zh: 純禮曰：「草濕則生火，何足怪！」

translations.literal: Chunli said: "Wet grass catches fire—what is there to wonder at!"
translations.idiomatic: Chunli said, "Damp hay can catch fire—what is so strange about that?"

sentences.zh: 但使密償之。

translations.literal: He merely had it secretly compensated.
translations.idiomatic: He simply had the loss quietly made good.

sentences.zh: 庫吏盜絲多罪至死，純禮曰：「以棼然之絲而殺之，吾不忍也。」

translations.literal: A warehouse clerk who stole silk faced a capital offense; Chunli said: "To put a man to death over a tangle of silk—I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: A warehouse clerk who had stolen silk faced the death penalty. Chunli said, "To execute a man over a few skeins of tangled silk—I cannot bring myself to do it."

sentences.zh: 聽其家趣買以贖，命釋其株連者。

translations.literal: He allowed the man's family to hurry and purchase silk to redeem him, and ordered those implicated by association to be released.
translations.idiomatic: He let the family rush to buy silk to redeem him, and ordered all those caught up in the case by association to be freed.

sentences.zh: 除戶部郎中、京西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Vice Transport Commissioner of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Ministry of Revenue and vice transport commissioner of Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，入為吏部郎中，遷左司。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanyou era he entered the capital as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and was transferred to the Left Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanyou reign he was recalled to the capital as director of the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to the Left Office of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 又遷太常少卿、江淮荊浙發運使。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Transport Commissioner for the Jiang-Huai, Jing, and Zhe regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and transport commissioner for the Jiang-Huai and Jing-Zhe circuits.

sentences.zh: 以光祿卿召，遷刑部侍郎，進給事中。

translations.literal: Summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice and promoted to Drafting Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, he was transferred to vice minister of justice and promoted to drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 純禮凡所封駁，正名分紀綱，皆國體之大者。

translations.literal: In all of Chunli's memorial rejections he corrected titles and upheld discipline—matters all of great import to the dignity of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Every rescript Chunli returned corrected improper titles and upheld institutional propriety—each one a matter of fundamental importance to the state's dignity.

sentences.zh: 張耒除起居舍人，病未能朝，而令先供職。

translations.literal: Zhang Lei was appointed Attendant of the Diaries of Activity and Repose; he was ill and unable to attend court, yet was ordered to assume his duties first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lei was appointed attendant of the diaries of activity and repose. Though too ill to attend court, he was told to take up his duties beforehand.

sentences.zh: 純禮批敕曰：「臣僚未有以疾謁告，不赴朝參先視事者。

translations.literal: Chunli wrote a rescript rejection, saying: "No official has ever reported illness and failed to attend court audience yet assumed duties first.
translations.idiomatic: Chunli returned the rescript with this objection: "No official has ever reported sick, skipped court audience, and begun work ahead of time.

sentences.zh: 耒能供職，豈不能見君？

translations.literal: If Lei can assume duties, how can he not see the ruler?
translations.idiomatic: If Lei is well enough to perform his duties, how can he be too ill to appear before the emperor?

sentences.zh: 壞禮亂法，所不當為。」

translations.literal: This violates ritual and disrupts law; it is what ought not to be done."
translations.idiomatic: This violates ritual propriety and undermines the law. It must not be permitted."

sentences.zh: 聞者皆悚動。

translations.literal: All who heard of it were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard of the rebuke were deeply stirred.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞擊執政，將遂代其位，先以諷純禮。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief attacked the chief ministers and was about to succeed to their positions; he first sounded Chunli out on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief was assailing the chief ministers with the aim of taking their posts, and he first tried to feel out Chunli's views.

sentences.zh: 純禮曰：「論人而奪之位，寧不避嫌邪？

translations.literal: Chunli said: "To discuss a man and seize his position—should one not avoid suspicion?
translations.idiomatic: Chunli said, "To criticize a man in order to take his place—should one not at least avoid the appearance of self-interest?

sentences.zh: 命果下，吾必還之。」

translations.literal: If the appointment is indeed issued, I shall certainly return it."
translations.idiomatic: If the appointment is actually issued to me, I shall certainly refuse it.

sentences.zh: 宰相即徙純禮刑部侍郎，而後出命。

translations.literal: The chief minister immediately transferred Chunli to Vice Minister of Justice, and only then issued the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister at once moved Chunli to vice minister of justice, and only then issued the new appointment.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部，改天章閣待制、樞密都承旨，去知亳州、提舉明道宮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, changed to Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and left office to govern Bozhou and oversee the Mingdao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, made attendant drafting academician of the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations and chief secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then left the capital to govern Bozhou and oversee the Mingdao Palace.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，以龍圖閣直學士知開封府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Chunli was made Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne, Chunli was appointed academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams and prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 前尹以刻深為治，純禮曰：「寬猛相濟，聖人之訓。

translations.literal: The previous prefect had governed with harsh severity. Chunli said: "Leniency and severity complement each other—this is the sage's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: The previous prefect had ruled with pitiless severity. Chunli said, "Leniency and severity should complement each other—that is the sage's teaching.

sentences.zh: 今處深文之後，若益以猛，是以火濟火也。

translations.literal: Now, coming after excessive legal severity, if one adds further severity, it is using fire to quench fire.
translations.idiomatic: After an era of harsh legalism, to pile on more severity is to fight fire with fire.

sentences.zh: 方務去前之苛，猶慮未盡，豈有寬為患也。」

translations.literal: We are just striving to remove the previous harshness and still worry it has not been fully removed—how could leniency be a harm?"
translations.idiomatic: We are still working to undo the previous harshness and fear we have not gone far enough—how could moderation itself be a danger?"

sentences.zh: 由是一切以寬處之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he handled everything with leniency.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he disposed of every case with a lighter hand.

sentences.zh: 中旨鞫享澤村民謀逆，純禮審其故，此民入戲場觀優，歸途見匠者作桶，取而戴於首曰：「與劉先生如何？」

translations.literal: An imperial order came to investigate villagers of Xiangze for plotting rebellion. Chunli examined the facts: this man had entered a theater to watch an opera; on the way home he saw a craftsman making a barrel, took it, and put it on his head, saying, "How does this compare with Master Liu?"
translations.idiomatic: An imperial directive ordered an inquiry into villagers of Xiangze on charges of treason. Chunli looked into the matter and found that the man had gone to a playhouse to watch a performance. On his way home he saw a cooper making a tub, picked it up, placed it on his head, and asked, "How do I look next to Master Liu?"

sentences.zh: 遂為匠擒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was seized by the craftsman.
translations.idiomatic: The cooper then seized him.

sentences.zh: 明日入對，徽宗問何以處之，對曰：「愚人村野無所知，若以叛逆蔽罪，恐辜好生之德，以不應為杖之，足矣。」

translations.literal: The next day he entered audience; Huizong asked how to deal with the case, and he replied: "This foolish villager knows nothing of the world. If we cover him with the crime of rebellion, I fear we would betray the virtue of cherishing life. To punish him for improper conduct with a beating is enough."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chunli appeared at court. Huizong asked how the case should be handled, and he replied, "The man is an ignorant country fellow. To charge him with treason would violate the principle of sparing life. A beating for improper conduct is punishment enough."

sentences.zh: 曰：「何以戒後人？」

translations.literal: Huizong said: "How then shall we warn those who come after?"
translations.idiomatic: Huizong asked, "But how will that serve as a warning to others?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「正欲外間知陛下刑憲不濫，足以為訓爾。」

translations.literal: He said: "Precisely because I wish outsiders to know that Your Majesty's punishments and laws are not applied indiscriminately— that alone is sufficient as a lesson."
translations.idiomatic: Chunli answered, "Precisely because I want the world to see that Your Majesty's punishments are measured and never abused—that in itself will be lesson enough."

sentences.zh: 徽宗從之。

translations.literal: Huizong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Huizong accepted his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部尚書，擢尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of rites and elevated to right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 侍御史陳次升乞除罷言官並自內批，不由三省進擬，右相曾布力爭不能得，乞降黜次升。

translations.literal: The Remonstrance Official Chen Cisheng requested that censorial officials be dismissed entirely by inner draft, without going through the Three Departments for nomination; the Right Chancellor Zeng Bu argued vigorously but could not prevail, and requested that Cisheng be demoted.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance official Chen Cisheng petitioned that censorial appointments be dismissed by direct imperial rescript, bypassing the Three Departments. Right Chancellor Zeng Bu fought the proposal hard but could not stop it, and asked that Cisheng himself be demoted.

sentences.zh: 純禮徐進曰：「次升何罪？

translations.literal: Chunli slowly advanced and said: "What crime has Cisheng committed?
translations.idiomatic: Chunli stepped forward calmly and asked, "What offense has Cisheng committed?

sentences.zh: 不過防柄臣各引所親，且去不附己者爾。」

translations.literal: Nothing more than guarding against powerful ministers each advancing their own favorites and removing those who do not attach themselves to them."
translations.idiomatic: Nothing more than preventing powerful ministers from installing their own partisans and purging those who refuse to follow them.

sentences.zh: 徽宗曰：「然。」

translations.literal: Huizong said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Huizong said, "That is so."

sentences.zh: 乃寢布議。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bu's proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu's proposal was set aside.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿告老，徽宗問執政，執政欲許之。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing requested retirement on grounds of age; Huizong asked the chief ministers, and the chief ministers wished to grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing asked to retire on account of old age. Huizong consulted the chief ministers, who were inclined to approve.

sentences.zh: 純禮曰：「惠卿嘗輔政，其人固不足重，然當存國體。」

translations.literal: Chunli said: "Huiqing once assisted in government; the man himself is surely not worth honoring, yet one ought to preserve the dignity of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Chunli said, "Huiqing once held high office. The man himself may not deserve esteem, but the dignity of the state must be preserved."

sentences.zh: 曾布奏：「議者多憂財用不足，此非所急也，願陛下勿以為慮。」

translations.literal: Zeng Bu memorialized: "Many in the discussions worry that finances are insufficient; this is not what is urgent—I hope Your Majesty will not be concerned."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu submitted a memorial: "Many officials worry about insufficient revenue, but that is not the pressing concern. I hope Your Majesty will not let it trouble you."

sentences.zh: 純禮曰：「古者無三年之蓄，曰國非其國。

translations.literal: Chunli said: "In antiquity, if there were not stores for three years, it was said the state was not a state.
translations.idiomatic: Chunli replied, "In antiquity it was said that a state without three years' worth of stores was no state at all.

sentences.zh: 今大農告匱，帑庾枵空，而曰不足慮，非面謾邪？」

translations.literal: Now the great granaries report depletion and the treasury granaries are empty, yet you say there is nothing to worry about—is this not deception to one's face?"
translations.idiomatic: Today the chief granaries stand depleted and the treasury coffers are bare, and yet you say there is no cause for concern—is that not bare-faced deceit?"

sentences.zh: 因從容諫曰：「邇者朝廷命令，莫不是元豐而非元祐。

translations.literal: He then calmly remonstrated, saying: "Recently the court's orders all praise the Yuans Feng era and condemn the Yuanyou era.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered a measured remonstrance: "Lately every court directive praises the Yuans Feng reforms and condemns the Yuanyou period.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，神宗立法之意固善，吏推行之，或有失當，以致病民。

translations.literal: In my view, the intent of Emperor Shenzong's laws was indeed good; when officials implemented them there were sometimes improprieties, causing harm to the people.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, Shenzong's legislative aims were fundamentally sound, but officials sometimes enforced them improperly and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 宣仁聽斷，一時小有潤色，蓋大臣識見異同，非必盡懷邪為私也。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanren held the reins of government, there were at the time small improvements, largely because the great ministers' views differed—not necessarily because all harbored evil for private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Dowager Xuanren's regency there were modest improvements, chiefly because leading ministers held different views—not because every opponent of the new laws acted from private malice.

sentences.zh: 今議論之臣，有不得志，故挾此藉口。

translations.literal: Now among the officials engaged in discussion, some have not achieved their ambitions, and therefore seize on this as a pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Today some of the officials driving this debate have failed to advance as they wished, and they are using the issue as a pretext.

sentences.zh: 以元豐為是，則欲賢元豐之人；

translations.literal: If Yuans Feng is held to be right, then they wish to exalt the men of Yuans Feng;
translations.idiomatic: If Yuans Feng is declared right, they want to elevate its partisans;

sentences.zh: 以元祐為非，則欲斥元祐之士，其心豈恤國事？

translations.literal: if the Yuanyou era is held wrong, then they wish to drive out the men of Yuanyou—do their hearts truly care about state affairs?
translations.idiomatic: if Yuanyou is declared wrong, they want to purge its adherents. Do they truly have the nation's welfare at heart?

sentences.zh: 直欲快私忿以售其奸，不可不深察也。」

translations.literal: They directly wish to indulge private resentment to achieve their scheming—this must be deeply examined."
translations.idiomatic: They mean only to vent private grudges and advance their own designs. Your Majesty must look into this with the greatest care."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「自古天下汨亂，系於用人。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since ancient times the disorder of the realm has hinged on the employment of men.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Since antiquity the rise and fall of empires has always turned on whom the throne chooses to employ.

sentences.zh: 祖宗於此，最得其要。

translations.literal: Our ancestors in this matter most grasped the essential point.
translations.idiomatic: Our founding emperors understood this better than anyone.

sentences.zh: 太祖用呂餘慶，太宗用王禹偁，真宗用張知白，皆從下列置諸要途。

translations.literal: Taizu employed Lü Yuqing, Taizong employed Wang Yucheng, and Zhenzong employed Zhang Zhibai—all were placed in important posts from lower ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu elevated Lü Yuqing, Taizong elevated Wang Yucheng, and Zhenzong elevated Zhang Zhibai—each plucked from modest station and set on the path to high office.

sentences.zh: 人君欲得英傑之心，固當不次飭拔。

translations.literal: If a ruler wishes to win the hearts of heroes and outstanding men, he ought indeed to promote them out of turn with extraordinary elevation.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler wishes to win the loyalty of exceptional talent, he must be willing to promote men out of turn and elevate them beyond ordinary procedure.

sentences.zh: 必待薦而後用，則守正特立之士，將終身晦跡矣。」

translations.literal: If one must wait for recommendation before employing them, then upright men who stand apart will hide their traces for a lifetime."
translations.idiomatic: If appointment always waits on recommendation, men of steadfast integrity who stand apart from the crowd will remain in obscurity all their lives.

sentences.zh: 左司諫江公望論繼述事當執中道，不可拘一偏。

translations.literal: Left Supervising Remonstrance Official Jiang Gongwang discussed the matter of policy succession and held that the middle Way should be maintained, and that one must not cling to a single bias.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gongwang, Left Supervising Remonstrance Official, submitted a memorial on policy succession arguing that the ruler should hold to the middle course and not be bound to one-sided positions.

sentences.zh: 徽宗出示其疏，純禮贊之曰：「願陛下以曉中外，使知聖意所向，亦足以革小人徇利之情。

translations.literal: Emperor Huizong displayed his memorial; Chunli praised it, saying: "I hope Your Majesty will make this known within and without, so that all may know where the sage mind is directed; this would also suffice to reform the sentiment of petty men who pursue profit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong showed the memorial at court. Chunli praised it, saying, "I pray Your Majesty will proclaim this far and wide, so that all within and beyond the palace may know the emperor's intent. That alone would be enough to check petty men who serve only their own gain.

sentences.zh: 乞褒遷公望，以勸來者。」

translations.literal: I beg that Gongwang be rewarded with promotion, to encourage those who come after."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Gongwang be honored with promotion, as an encouragement to others who may speak forth in future."

sentences.zh: 純禮沉毅剛正，曾布憚之，激駙馬都尉王詵曰：「上欲除君承旨，范右丞不可。」

translations.literal: Chunli was deep, resolute, and upright; Zeng Bu feared him and incited Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Wang Shen, saying: "The emperor wishes to remove you as drafting attendant; Vice Director Fan will not permit it."
translations.idiomatic: Chunli was grave, resolute, and upright in character. Zeng Bu feared him and goaded Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Wang Shen, saying, "The emperor means to remove you from the drafting post, but Vice Director Fan will not allow it."

sentences.zh: 詵怒。

translations.literal: Shen grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: Shen flew into a rage.

sentences.zh: 會詵館遼使，純禮主宴，詵誣其輒斥御名，罷為端明殿學士、知潁昌府，提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: When Shen was hosting Liao envoys, Chunli presided over the banquet; Shen falsely accused him of abruptly using the imperial name and had him dismissed to Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, Prefect of Yingchang, and Supervisor of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen was playing host to Liao envoys, Chunli presided at the banquet. Shen falsely accused him of having uttered the emperor's name without proper formality. Chunli was dismissed from office, made Academician of the Hall of Bright Clarity, appointed prefect of Yingchang, and given charge of Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 崇寧中，啟黨禁，貶試少府監，分司南京。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era, when the factional ban was revived, he was demoted to probationary Director of the Palace Workshops with nominal service at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era, when factional proscriptions were renewed, he was demoted to probationary Director of the Palace Workshops and assigned nominal duty at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 又貶靜江軍節度副使，徐州安置，徙單州。

translations.literal: He was further demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, placed under supervision at Xuzhou, and transferred to Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted to Vice Military Commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, placed under restricted residence at Xuzhou, and then moved to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，復左朝議大夫，提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was restored to Left Policy Advisor and given charge of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign he was restored to Left Policy Advisor and put in charge of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十六。

translations.literal: He died, at the age of seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 子 純粹

translations.literal: Son: Chuncui
translations.idiomatic: His son Chuncui

sentences.zh: 純粹，字德孺，以蔭遷至贊善大夫、檢正中書刑房，與同列有爭，出知滕縣，遷提舉成都諸路茶場。

translations.literal: Chuncui, styled Deru, through hereditary privilege rose to Gentleman Attendant and Inspector in the Criminal Section of the Secretariat-Chancellery; he quarreled with colleagues, was sent out as Prefect of Teng County, and was promoted to Supervisor of Tea Markets on the various routes of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Chuncui, styled Deru, entered service through hereditary privilege and rose to Gentleman Attendant and inspector in the Secretariat's criminal section. After a dispute with colleagues he was sent out as magistrate of Teng County, then promoted to supervisor of the tea markets on the Chengdu circuits.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，為陝西轉運判官。

translations.literal: During the Yuanfeng era, he served as Transport Assessor of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanfeng reign he was made transport assessor for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時五路出師伐西夏：高遵裕出環慶，劉昌祚出涇原，李憲出熙河，种諤出鄜延，王中正出河東。

translations.literal: At that time five routes sent armies to attack Western Xia: Gao Zunyu from Huanqing, Liu Changzuo from Jingyuan, Li Xian from Xihe, Zhong E from Fuyan, and Wang Zhongzheng from Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: At that time five army columns marched against Western Xia: Gao Zunyu from the Huanqing circuit, Liu Changzuo from Jingyuan, Li Xian from Xihe, Zhong E from Fuyan, and Wang Zhongzheng from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 遵裕怒昌祚後期，欲按誅之，昌祚憂恚病臥，其麾下皆憤焉。

translations.literal: Zunyu was angry that Changzuo was late and wished to investigate and execute him; Changzuo fell ill with grief and indignation, and his subordinates were all enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyu was furious that Changzuo had arrived late and sought to have him tried and executed. Changzuo fell ill with grief and resentment, and his officers seethed with anger.

sentences.zh: 純粹恐兩軍不協，致生他變，勸遵裕往問昌祚疾，其難遂解。

translations.literal: Chuncui feared that disharmony between the two armies would give rise to other disturbances, and urged Zunyu to visit Changzuo in his illness; the difficulty was then resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that discord between the two armies might spark further trouble, Chuncui persuaded Zunyu to pay a sick visit to Changzuo, and the crisis passed.

sentences.zh: 神宗責諸將無功，謀欲再舉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong reproached the generals for achieving nothing and planned to launch another campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong rebuked the generals for their lack of success and planned a renewed campaign.

sentences.zh: 純粹奏：「關陝事力單竭，公私大困，若復加騷動，根本可憂。

translations.literal: Chuncui memorialized: "The strength of Guanzhong and Shaanxi is utterly exhausted, and both public and private affairs are in great distress; if further disturbance is added, the foundation may be endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Chuncui submitted a memorial: "Guanzhong and Shaanxi have been drained to the last measure. Public and private resources alike are exhausted. If the region is stirred up again, the very foundations of the realm may be shaken.

sentences.zh: 異時言者必職臣是咎，臣寧受盡言之罪於今日，不忍默默以貽後悔。」

translations.literal: When others speak of this hereafter, they will surely blame this minister; I would rather receive the penalty of speaking fully today than remain silent and leave regrets."
translations.idiomatic: When men speak of this later, they will surely blame me. I would rather accept every penalty for speaking out today than hold my peace and leave cause for regret."

sentences.zh: 神宗納之，進為副使。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this and promoted him to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heeded him and promoted Chuncui to vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 吳居厚為京東轉運使，數獻羨賦。

translations.literal: Wu Juhou served as Transport Commissioner of Jingdong and repeatedly presented surplus tax revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Juhou, transport commissioner of Jingdong, repeatedly reported surplus revenue to the throne.

sentences.zh: 神宗將以徐州大錢二十萬緡助陝西，純粹語其僚曰：「吾部雖急，忍復取此膏血之餘？」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to use two hundred thousand strings of large coin from Xuzhou to aid Shaanxi; Chuncui said to his staff: "Though my circuit is in distress, how can I bear to take again what remains of the people's lifeblood?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor proposed sending two hundred thousand strings of large coin from Xuzhou to aid Shaanxi, Chuncui told his staff, "Though our own circuit is hard pressed, how can we take what little remains of the people's blood and sweat?"

sentences.zh: 即奏：「本路得錢誠為利，自徐至邊，勞費甚矣。」

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized: "For this circuit to obtain the funds would indeed be a benefit, but from Xuzhou to the frontier the labor and expense would be very great."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately memorialized: "It would certainly benefit our circuit to receive these funds, but the cost of moving them from Xuzhou to the border would be enormous."

sentences.zh: 懇辭弗受。

translations.literal: He earnestly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly declined and refused the money.

sentences.zh: 入為右司郎中。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Office Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as director in the Right Office of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，居厚敗，命純粹以直龍圖閣往代之，盡革其苛政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Juhou fell from power; Chuncui was ordered to go in his place as Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images and completely reformed his harsh policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne and Juhou was disgraced, Chuncui was sent in his stead as Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images and abolished every harsh policy Juhou had left behind.

sentences.zh: 時蘇軾自登州召還，純粹與軾同建募役之議，軾謂純粹講此事尤為精詳。

translations.literal: At that time Su Shi was recalled from Deng Prefecture; Chuncui and Shi together drafted the proposal on hired labor service, and Shi said that Chuncui's exposition of the matter was especially thorough and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi was then recalled from Deng Prefecture. Chuncui joined him in drafting the hired-service proposal, and Su remarked that Chuncui's treatment of the subject was especially precise and thorough.

sentences.zh: 復代兄純仁知慶州。

translations.literal: He again replaced his elder brother Chunren as Prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He again replaced his elder brother Chunren as prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 時與夏議分疆界，純粹請棄所取夏地，曰：「爭地未棄，則邊隙無時可除。

translations.literal: At that time he was negotiating with Xia over the boundary; Chuncui asked to abandon the Xia territory that had been taken, saying: "As long as disputed land is not abandoned, border friction cannot be removed at any time.
translations.idiomatic: While negotiating the border with Western Xia, Chuncui urged that captured Xia territory be returned, saying, "So long as disputed lands are held, border conflict will never end.

sentences.zh: 如河東之葭蘆、吳堡，鄜延之米脂、羲合、浮圖，環慶之安疆，深在夏境，於漢界地利形勢，略無所益。

translations.literal: Such places as Jialu and Wubao in Hedong, Mizhi, Yihe, and Futu in Fuyan, and Anjiang in Huanqing lie deep within Xia territory and offer virtually no advantage to Han territory in terrain or strategic position.
translations.idiomatic: Places such as Jialu and Wubao in Hedong, Mizhi, Yihe, and Futu in Fuyan, and Anjiang in Huanqing lie deep inside Xia territory. They confer scarcely any strategic advantage on our side of the border.

sentences.zh: 而蘭、會之地，耗蠹尤深，不可不棄。」

translations.literal: As for the territory of Lan and Hui, the drain of resources is especially deep, and it must be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: The Lan and Hui regions, above all, bleed the treasury dry and must be given up."

sentences.zh: 所言皆略施行。

translations.literal: What he said was all more or less put into effect.
translations.idiomatic: His recommendations were largely adopted.

sentences.zh: 純粹又言：「諸路策應，舊制也。

translations.literal: Chuncui also said: "Mutual support among circuits was the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Chuncui further argued that coordinated relief among circuits had been the established practice.

sentences.zh: 自徐禧罷策應，若夏兵大舉，一路攻圍，力有不勝，而鄰路拱手坐觀，其不拔者幸爾。

translations.literal: Since Xu Xi abolished mutual support, if Xia troops come in force and one route is besieged and cannot prevail, neighboring routes will sit by with folded hands—and only by luck will the place not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Xu Xi ended cross-circuit support, if Xia forces strike in strength and one circuit is besieged beyond its capacity to resist, neighboring circuits have stood by idle. When a fortress has not fallen, it has been mere good fortune.

sentences.zh: 今宜修明戰守救援之法。」

translations.literal: Now one ought to clarify the methods of fighting, defending, and coming to one another's aid."
translations.idiomatic: The court should now restore clear rules for combat, defense, and mutual rescue.

sentences.zh: 朝廷是之。

translations.literal: The court approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 及夏侵涇原，純粹遣將曲珍救之，曰：「本道首建應援牽制之策，臣子之義，忘軀徇國，無謂鄰路被寇，非我職也。」

translations.literal: When Xia invaded Jingyuan, Chuncui sent the general Qu Zhen to the rescue, saying: "This circuit was the first to propose the strategy of mutual support and diversion; the duty of a minister is to forget his person and serve the state—do not think that when a neighboring route is attacked, it is not my office."
translations.idiomatic: When Xia forces invaded Jingyuan, Chuncui dispatched General Qu Zhen to relieve the siege, saying, "This circuit pioneered the policy of coordinated support and diversion. A minister's duty is to forget himself for the state. Do not imagine that a neighbor under attack is someone else's concern."

sentences.zh: 珍即日疾馳三百里，破之于曲律，搗橫山，夏眾遁去。

translations.literal: Zhen that same day raced three hundred li, defeated the enemy at Qülü, struck at Hengshan, and the Xia forces fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zhen rode hard three hundred li that very day, routed the enemy at Qülü, raided Hengshan, and drove the Xia army off.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，除寶文閣待制，再任，召為戶部侍郎，又出知延州。

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou era, he was made Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Precious Culture, served a second term, was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue, and again went out as Prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanyou he was made Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Precious Culture. After a second term in Qing he was recalled as vice minister of revenue, then sent out again as prefect of Yan.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shaosheng reign.

sentences.zh: 哲宗親政，用事者欲開邊釁，御史郭知章遂論純粹元祐棄地事，降直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: When Zhezong personally took the reins of government, those in power wished to provoke border conflict; Censor Guo Zhizhang thereupon impeached Chuncui over the Yuanyou land-abandonment affair, and he was demoted from Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhezong took personal control, the faction in power sought to stir up border trouble. Censor Guo Zhizhang impeached Chuncui over the Yuanyou land abandonments, and he was demoted from Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images.

sentences.zh: 明年，復以寶文閣待制知熙州。

translations.literal: The next year, he was again made Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Precious Culture and Prefect of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was restored as Attendant Drafting Academician and made prefect of Xi.

sentences.zh: 章惇、蔡卞經略西夏，疑純粹不與共事，改知鄧州。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun and Cai Bian were conducting operations against Western Xia; suspecting that Chuncui would not work with them, he was transferred to Prefect of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun and Cai Bian were directing operations against Western Xia. Doubting that Chuncui would cooperate, the court moved him to prefect of Deng.

sentences.zh: 曆河南府、滑州，旋以元祐黨人奪職，知均州。

translations.literal: He served successively at Henan Prefecture and Hua Prefecture; soon, as a Yuanyou factionalist, he was stripped of rank and made Prefect of Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served at Henan Prefecture and Hua in turn, but was soon stripped of rank as a Yuanyou factionalist and posted to Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，起知信州，復故職，知太原，加龍圖閣直學士，再臨延州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended the throne, Chuncui was raised to Prefect of Xin Prefecture, his former rank was restored, he was made Prefect of Taiyuan, promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Images, and again took charge of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne, Chuncui was rehabilitated as prefect of Xin, his former title restored, and he was posted to Taiyuan. Promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Images, he once again took charge of Yan.

sentences.zh: 改知永興軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 尋以言者落職，知金州，提舉鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Soon, on the words of critics, he was stripped of rank, made Prefect of Jin Prefecture, and given charge of Hongqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long critics brought about his dismissal from rank; he was made prefect of Jin and given nominal charge of Hongqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 又責常州別駕，鄂州安置，錮子弟不得擅入都。

translations.literal: He was further punished as Assistant Prefect of Chang Prefecture, placed under supervision at E Prefecture, and his sons and younger brothers were forbidden to enter the capital without permission.
translations.idiomatic: He was further demoted to assistant prefect of Chang, placed under restricted residence at E Prefecture, and his sons and brothers were barred from entering the capital without permission.

sentences.zh: 會赦，復領祠。

translations.literal: When an amnesty occurred, he again received a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty restored him to a nominal temple post.

sentences.zh: 久之，以右文殿修撰提舉太清宮。

translations.literal: After a long while, as Compiler of the Hall for Cultivating Culture he was given charge of the Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made Compiler of the Hall for Cultivating Culture and put in charge of the Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 黨禁解，復徽猷閣待制，致仕。

translations.literal: When the factional ban was lifted, his Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Designs was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: When the factional proscription was lifted, his title of Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Brilliant Designs was restored and he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: He died, at over seventy years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 純粹沉毅有幹略，才應時須，嘗論賣官之濫，以為：「國法固許進納取官，然未嘗聽其理選。

translations.literal: Chuncui was deep, resolute, and possessed of capacity and strategy; his talents met the needs of the age. Once, in discussing the abuse of selling offices, he said: "The laws of the state do indeed permit advancement through contribution to obtain office,
translations.idiomatic: Chuncui was grave, resolute, and resourceful; his talents were equal to the demands of his age. Once, criticizing the abuse of selling offices, he wrote: "The laws of the realm do permit men to obtain rank through monetary contribution,

sentences.zh: 今西北三路，許納三千二百緡買齋郎，四千六百緡買供奉職，並免試注官。

translations.literal: Now on the three northwestern routes, one may pay three thousand two hundred strings to buy a Supplicant rank, and four thousand six hundred strings to buy an Attendant-in-Waiting post, both exempt from examination for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet on the three northwestern circuits, three thousand two hundred strings now buys a Supplicant rank and four thousand six hundred strings buys an Attendant-in-Waiting post, both without examination or competitive appointment.

sentences.zh: 夫天下士大夫服勤至於垂死，不沾世恩，其富民猾商，捐錢千萬，則可任三子，切為朝廷惜之。」

translations.literal: The empire's scholar-officials toil until death yet receive no favor from the throne, while wealthy merchants who contribute millions may place three sons in office—in this I deeply grieve for the court."
translations.idiomatic: Scholar-officials throughout the empire labor until death without ever tasting imperial favor, while wealthy merchants who pay out millions may place three sons in office at once. The court's loss in this is grievous.

sentences.zh: 疏上，不聽。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, it went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 凡論事剴切類此。

translations.literal: In all his remonstrances he was incisive in this manner.
translations.idiomatic: In every memorial he submitted, his language was as forthright and penetrating as this.

sentences.zh: 范純仁

translations.literal: Fan Chunren
translations.idiomatic: Fan Chunren

sentences.zh: 純仁，字堯夫，其始生之夕，母李氏夢兒墮月中，承以衣裾，得之，遂生純仁。

translations.literal: Chunren, styled Yaofu—on the night he was born, his mother Lady Li dreamed that a child fell from the moon; she caught him in her skirt hem, and Chunren was born.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren, styled Yaofu, was born on the night his mother, Lady Li, dreamed that a child fell from the moon into the fold of her skirt. She caught the child, and Chunren was born.

sentences.zh: 資警悟，八歲，能講所授書。

translations.literal: He was quick and perceptive; at eight he could expound the books he had been taught.
translations.idiomatic: He was bright and quick-witted. At eight he could lecture on the texts he had been taught.

sentences.zh: 以父任為太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's office he was appointed assistant director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 中皇祐元年進士第，調知武進縣，以遠親不赴；

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examinations in the first year of Huangyou and was assigned as Prefect of Wujin County, but did not take up the post because the place was far from home;
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the first year of Huangyou and was assigned to Wujin County, but declined because the post was too far from home.

sentences.zh: 易長葛，又不往。

translations.literal: he was reassigned to Changge and again did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Changge and again refused to go.

sentences.zh: 仲淹曰：「汝昔日以遠為言，今近矣，復何辭？」

translations.literal: Zhongyan said: "You once pleaded distance as your reason; now the post is near—what excuse remains?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan said, "You once pleaded that the post was too far away. Now it is near—what reason can you give?"

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「豈可重於祿食，而輕去父母邪？

translations.literal: Chunren said: "How can one value salary and sustenance above leaving one's parents?
translations.idiomatic: Chunren replied, "How can I value salary and office above abandoning my parents?

sentences.zh: 雖近，亦不能遂養焉。」

translations.literal: Even though it is near, I still cannot go and support them."
translations.idiomatic: Even though the post is close, I still cannot leave them to take it."

sentences.zh: 仲淹門下多賢士，如胡瑗、孫復、石介、李覯之徙，純仁皆與從遊。

translations.literal: Many worthy scholars were among Zhongyan's followers, such as Hu Yuan, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, and Li Gou; Chunren studied with them all.
translations.idiomatic: Many eminent scholars gathered at Zhongyan's door—Hu Yuan, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, Li Gou, and others—and Chunren studied alongside them all.

sentences.zh: 晝夜肄業，至夜分不寢，置燈帳中，帳頂如墨色。

translations.literal: He applied himself day and night to his studies, not sleeping until the middle watch; he kept his lamp inside a tent, and the top of the tent turned black as ink.
translations.idiomatic: He studied day and night without rest, often keeping at his books until the middle watch. He read by lamplight inside a tent, and the tent's peak turned black with soot.

sentences.zh: 仲俺沒，始出仕，以著作佐郎知襄城縣。

translations.literal: When Zhongyan died, Chunren at last entered office, and as Editorial Assistant he was made Prefect of Xiangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Zhongyan's death did Chunren enter official life. As editorial assistant he was appointed magistrate of Xiangcheng County.

sentences.zh: 兄純祐有心疾，奉之如父，藥膳居服，皆躬親時節之。

translations.literal: His elder brother Chunyou suffered from a mental disorder; Chunren served him as though he were a father, personally attending to his medicine, food, and mourning garments at the proper seasons.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Chunyou suffered from a mental illness. Chunren cared for him as though he were a father, personally seeing to his medicine, meals, and mourning dress at every season.

sentences.zh: 賈昌朝守北都，請參幕府，以兄辭。

translations.literal: Jia Changchao, prefect of the Northern Capital, invited him to join his staff, but he declined on account of his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Changchao, prefect of the Northern Capital, invited him into his staff, but Chunren declined because of his brother.

sentences.zh: 宋庠薦試館職，謝曰：「輦轂之下，非兄養疾地也。」

translations.literal: Song Kui recommended him for the palace examination for archival posts; he declined, saying: "Within the imperial precincts is no place for me to nurse my brother's illness."
translations.idiomatic: Song Kui recommended him for the palace examination leading to archival posts. Chunren declined, saying, "The capital is no place to tend a sick brother."

sentences.zh: 富弼責之曰：「臺閣之任豈易得？

translations.literal: Fu Bi rebuked him, saying: "A post in the palace archives—is it so easily obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi reproached him: "A post in the palace archives is not so easily won—why treat it so lightly?

sentences.zh: 何庸如是。」

translations.literal: Why be so obstinate?"
translations.idiomatic: Why be so stubborn?"

sentences.zh: 卒不就。

translations.literal: In the end he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not accept.

sentences.zh: 襄城民不蠶織，勸使植桑，有罪而情輕者，視所植多寡除其罰，民益賴慕，後呼為「著作林」。

translations.literal: The people of Xiangcheng did not raise silkworms or weave; he urged them to plant mulberry trees, and for offenders whose crimes were minor he reduced punishment according to how many trees they had planted; the people came to rely on and admire him, and later called him the "Grove of the Editorial Assistant."
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xiangcheng did not raise silkworms or weave cloth. Chunren urged them to plant mulberry trees and, for minor offenders, reduced their penalties in proportion to how many trees they planted. The people came to trust and admire him, and later called the place the "Grove of the Editorial Assistant."

sentences.zh: 兄死，葬洛陽。

translations.literal: When his brother died, he buried him in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother died, he buried him in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 韓琦、富弼貽書洛尹，使助其葬，既葬，尹訝不先聞。

translations.literal: Han Qi and Fu Bi wrote to the Luoyang prefect asking him to assist with the funeral; after the burial, the prefect was surprised that he had not been told beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and Fu Bi wrote to the prefect of Luoyang asking him to help with the funeral. After the burial the prefect was astonished that he had not been told in advance.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「私室力足辦，豈宜慁公為哉？」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "My family's means were sufficient for the task—how could I trouble a public official for it?"
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "My family's resources were enough to manage the funeral. How could I impose on a public official?"

sentences.zh: 簽書許州觀察判官、知襄邑縣。

translations.literal: He served as Signing Secretary and Administrative Assistant under the Prefectural Observation Commissioner of Xu Prefecture, and as Prefect of Xiangyi County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as signing secretary and administrative assistant under the observation commissioner of Xu Prefecture, and as magistrate of Xiangyi County.

sentences.zh: 縣有牧地，衛士牧馬，以踐民稼，純仁捕一人杖之。

translations.literal: The county had pasture land where palace guards pastured horses; they trampled the people's crops, and Chunren seized one man and had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The county contained pasture land where palace guards pastured their horses, trampling the people's crops. Chunren seized one of the guards and had him beaten.

sentences.zh: 牧地初不隸縣，主者怒曰：「天子宿衛，令敢爾邪？」

translations.literal: The pasture had not originally been under county jurisdiction; the person in charge grew angry and said: "These are the emperor's personal guards—how dare a magistrate act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: The pasture had not originally fallen under county jurisdiction. Its superintendent flew into a rage: "These are the emperor's own guards—how dare a county magistrate treat them so?"

sentences.zh: 白其事於上，劾治甚急。

translations.literal: He reported the matter to the throne, and an impeachment was pressed with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the matter upward, and an impeachment was pressed with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「養兵出於稅畝，若使暴民田而不得問，稅安所出？」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Maintaining troops comes from the tax on every mu of land; if they may ravage the people's fields with impunity, from what will taxes come?"
translations.idiomatic: Chunren replied, "The army is maintained from taxes levied on every plot of land. If soldiers may trample the people's fields without consequence, whence will those taxes come?"

sentences.zh: 詔釋之，且聽牧地隸縣。

translations.literal: An edict released the man and also permitted pasture land to come under county jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the man released and permitted pasture lands to be placed under county jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 凡牧地隸縣，自純仁始。

translations.literal: In all cases of pasture land coming under county jurisdiction, this began with Chunren.
translations.idiomatic: The practice of placing pasture lands under county jurisdiction began with Chunren.

sentences.zh: 時旱久不雨，純仁籍境內賈舟，諭之曰：「民將無食，爾所販五穀，貯之佛寺，候食闕時吾為糴之。」

translations.literal: At that time drought had long continued without rain; Chunren registered the merchant boats within his jurisdiction and instructed them: "The people will soon have no food; store the grain you trade in Buddhist temples, and when food runs short I will buy it from you."
translations.idiomatic: A long drought had brought no rain. Chunren registered every merchant boat in his jurisdiction and told the traders: "The people will soon have nothing to eat. Store the grain you carry in Buddhist temples, and when food runs short I will purchase it from you."

sentences.zh: 眾賈從命，所蓄十數萬斛。

translations.literal: The merchants obeyed, and what they stored amounted to several hundred thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: The merchants complied, and the grain they stored amounted to several hundred thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 至春，諸縣皆饑，獨境內民不知也。

translations.literal: When spring came, all the neighboring counties were in famine, yet the people within his jurisdiction did not even know it.
translations.idiomatic: When spring came, every neighboring county was in famine, yet the people within his jurisdiction scarcely knew hunger at all.

sentences.zh: 治平中，擢江東轉運判官，召為殿中侍御史，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era he was promoted to Transport Assessor of Jiangdong, summoned as Attendant Censor in the Palace, and transferred to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping reign he was promoted to transport assessor of Jiangdong, recalled as attendant censor in the palace, and transferred to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 時方議濮王典禮，宰相韓琦、參知政事歐陽修等議尊崇之。

translations.literal: At that time the court was debating the rites due to the Prince of Pu; Chief Minister Han Qi, Vice Director Ouyang Xiu, and others argued for honoring him with elevated titles.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then debating the rites due to the Prince of Pu. Chief Minister Han Qi, Vice Director Ouyang Xiu, and others argued that he should be honored with elevated titles.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士王珪等議，宜如先朝追贈期親尊屬故事。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others argued that the precedent of posthumous enfeoffment for close relatives of the previous reign should be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others held that the precedent of posthumous enfeoffment for close relatives of the previous reign should be followed.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「陛下受命仁宗而為之子，與前代定策入繼之主異，宜如王珪等議。」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Your Majesty received the mandate from Renzong and became his son; this differs from earlier emperors who entered the succession through a fixed enthronement plan. The proposal of Wang Gui and the others should be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren argued: "Your Majesty received the throne from Renzong and became his son. That differs from earlier emperors who entered the succession through a predetermined enthronement plan. Wang Gui's proposal should be adopted."

sentences.zh: 繼與御史呂誨等更論奏，不聽。

translations.literal: He then joined Supervising Censor Lü Hui and others in further memorials, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Supervising Censor Lü Hui and others in further memorials, but the emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 純仁還所授告敕，家居待罪。

translations.literal: Chunren returned the commission and patent he had received and remained at home awaiting punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren returned the commission and patent he had received and remained at home awaiting punishment.

sentences.zh: 既而皇太后手書尊王為皇，夫人為後。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Empress Dowager issued a handwritten edict elevating the Prince to emperor and his consort to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Empress Dowager issued a handwritten edict elevating the Prince of Pu to emperor and his consort to empress.

sentences.zh: 純仁復言：「陛下以長君臨禦，奈何使命出房闈，異日或為權臣矯托之地，非人主自安計。」

translations.literal: Chunren spoke again: "Your Majesty governs as the senior sovereign—how can orders issue from the inner quarters? In days to come this may become ground for powerful ministers to forge edicts in their own interest. That is no plan by which a ruler may secure himself."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren spoke again: "Your Majesty governs as the senior sovereign—how can edicts issue from the inner quarters? In time to come this may become ground for powerful ministers to forge orders in their own interest. That is no plan by which a ruler can secure himself."

sentences.zh: 尋詔罷追尊，起純仁就職。

translations.literal: Soon an edict halted the posthumous elevation, and Chunren was recalled to office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict halted the posthumous elevation, and Chunren was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 純仁請出不已，遂通判安州，改知蘄州。

translations.literal: Chunren repeatedly requested to leave office and would not cease; he was finally made Vice Prefect of An Prefecture and transferred to Prefect of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren repeatedly asked to leave office and would not be dissuaded. He was finally made vice prefect of An and transferred to prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 曆京西提點刑獄、京西陝西轉運副使。

translations.literal: He served successively as Judicial Intendant of Jingxi and Vice Transport Commissioner of Jingxi and Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as judicial intendant of Jingxi and vice transport commissioner of the Jingxi and Shaanxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 召還，神宗問陝西城郭、甲兵、糧儲如何，對曰：「城郭粗全，甲兵粗修，糧儲粗備。」

translations.literal: Recalled to the capital, Emperor Shenzong asked how the walled cities, armor and weapons, and grain stores of Shaanxi stood; he replied: "The walled cities are roughly intact, armor and weapons roughly maintained, and grain stores roughly supplied."
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, Emperor Shenzong asked about the walled cities, armor, weapons, and grain stores of Shaanxi. Chunren replied, "The walled cities are roughly intact, armor and weapons roughly maintained, and grain stores roughly supplied."

sentences.zh: 神宗愕然曰：「卿之才朕所倚信，何為皆言粗？」

translations.literal: The emperor was startled and said: "Your talent is what I rely upon and trust—why do you say only 'roughly'?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled. "Your talent is what I rely on," he said. "Why do you answer only with 'roughly'?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「粗者未精之辭，如是足矣。

translations.literal: He replied: "'Roughly' means not yet refined; that is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren replied, "'Roughly' means not yet perfected—and that is sufficient.

sentences.zh: 願陛下且無留意邊功，若邊臣觀望，將為他日意外之患。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will for the present not fix your mind on frontier achievements; if frontier officials watch for opportunity, it will become an unforeseen calamity hereafter."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will for now set aside thoughts of frontier glory. If border officials begin watching for chances to advance themselves, that will breed unforeseen trouble in days to come."

sentences.zh: 拜兵部員外郎，兼起居舍人、同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of War, concurrently Attendant of the Diaries of Activity and Repose and Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice minister of war, concurrently attendant of the diaries of activity and repose and associate director of the remonstrance bureau.

sentences.zh: 奏言：「王安石變祖宗法度，掊克財利，民心不寧。

translations.literal: He memorialized, saying: "Wang Anshi has altered the laws and institutions of the ancestors, squeezed out wealth and profit, and the hearts of the people are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Wang Anshi has altered the laws and institutions of the ancestors, wrung profit from the people, and left the hearts of the realm unsettled.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：'怨豈在明，不見是圖。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: 'Is resentment found only in what is visible? One must plan for what is not seen.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says, 'Is resentment found only in what is visible? One must plan for what is not seen.'

sentences.zh: '願陛下圖不見之怨。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will plan for resentment that is not seen."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will heed the resentment that has not yet come into view.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「何謂不見之怨？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What is meant by resentment that is not seen?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "What do you mean by resentment that is not seen?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「杜牧所謂'天下之人，不敢言而敢怒'是也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "It is what Du Mu called 'the people of the empire dare not speak, yet dare to rage.'
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "It is what Du Mu meant when he wrote that the people of the empire dare not speak out, yet dare to seethe in silence."

sentences.zh: 神宗嘉納之，曰：「卿善論事，宜為朕條古今治亂可為監戒者。」

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this, saying: "You speak well on affairs of state; you should set forth for me, item by item, examples from past and present of order and disorder that may serve as warnings."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and said, "You argue well on affairs of state. Set forth for me, item by item, examples from past and present of order and disorder that may serve as warnings."

sentences.zh: 乃作《尚書解》以進，曰：「其言，皆堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之事也。

translations.literal: He thereupon composed the Exegesis of the Documents and presented it, saying: "Its words are all the deeds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon composed his Exegesis of the Documents and presented it, saying, "Its words are all the deeds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu.

sentences.zh: 治天下無以易此，願深究而力行之。」

translations.literal: There is nothing with which to replace this in governing the empire; I pray Your Majesty will study it deeply and put it vigorously into practice."
translations.idiomatic: There is nothing with which to replace this in governing the empire. I pray Your Majesty will study it deeply and put it vigorously into practice."

sentences.zh: 加直集賢院、同修起居注。

translations.literal: He was further made Direct Associate of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and Co-compiler of the Diaries of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Direct Associate of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and co-compiler of the diaries of activity and repose.

sentences.zh: 神宗切於求治，多延見疏逖小臣，咨訪闕失。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong was eager in his pursuit of good governance and often extended audiences to memorialists of humble rank, consulting them on shortcomings and failures.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong was eager for good governance and often granted audiences to humble memorialists from afar, consulting them on shortcomings in policy.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「小人之言，聽之若可采，行之必有累。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "The words of petty men, if listened to, seem adoptable, but if put into practice will surely bring harm.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren warned: "The words of petty men, if listened to, seem worth adopting, but if put into practice they will surely bring harm.

sentences.zh: 蓋知小忘大，貪近昧遠，願加深察。」

translations.literal: They know the small and forget the large, grasp what is near and obscure what is far—I pray Your Majesty will examine this more deeply."
translations.idiomatic: They grasp the small and forget the large, covet what is near and lose sight of what is far. I pray Your Majesty will examine such counsel more deeply."

sentences.zh: 富弼在相位，稱疾家居。

translations.literal: Fu Bi held office as chief minister but claimed illness and remained at home.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi held office as chief minister but claimed illness and remained at home.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「弼受三朝眷倚，當自任天下之重，而恤己深於恤物，憂疾過於憂邦，致主處身，二者胥失。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Bi received the trust of three reigns and ought to take upon himself the weight of the empire; yet he cares for himself more deeply than for others, and grieves over his illness more than over the state—in serving his ruler and conducting himself, he has failed in both.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren wrote: "Bi enjoyed the trust of three reigns and ought to have shouldered the weight of the empire. Yet he cares for himself more deeply than for the realm and grieves over his illness more than over the state. In serving his ruler and in his personal conduct, he has failed in both.

sentences.zh: 弼與先臣素厚，臣在諫省，不錄私謁以致忠告，願示以此章，使之自省。」

translations.literal: Bi and my late father were close, and I am in the remonstrance office—I do not record private visits in order to offer loyal counsel. I pray that this memorial be shown to him, that he may examine himself."
translations.idiomatic: Bi was close to my late father, and I serve in the remonstrance office, where I do not record private audiences in order to speak candidly. I ask that this memorial be shown to him, that he may examine himself."

sentences.zh: 又論呂誨不當罷御史中丞，李師中不可守邊。

translations.literal: He also argued that Lü Hui should not have been removed as Censor-in-Chief and that Li Shizhong should not be entrusted with frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Lü Hui should not have been removed as censor-in-chief and that Li Shizhong was unfit to hold a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 及薛向任發運使，行均輸法于六路。

translations.literal: When Xue Xiang was appointed Grain Transport Commissioner and implemented the balanced-transport system on six routes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Xiang was appointed grain transport commissioner and implemented the balanced-transport system on six circuits.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「臣嘗親奉德音，欲修先王補助之政。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "I once personally received the sage edict expressing the wish to restore the policy of aid and relief practiced by the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren wrote: "I once personally received the sage edict expressing the wish to restore the policy of aid and relief practiced by the former kings.

sentences.zh: 今乃效桑羊均輸之法，而使小人為之，掊克生靈，斂怨基禍。

translations.literal: Now the balanced-transport method of Sang Hongyang is being imitated and petty men are put in charge of it, squeezing the living and heaping up resentment—the foundation of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Now the court imitates Sang Hongyang's balanced-transport method and puts petty men in charge of it, squeezing the people and heaping up resentment—the very foundation of calamity.

sentences.zh: 安石以富國強兵之術，啟迪上心，欲求近功，忘其舊學。

translations.literal: Anshi, with his methods for enriching the state and strengthening the army, has opened the emperor's mind; seeking quick results, he has forgotten his earlier learning.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi, with his methods for enriching the state and strengthening the army, has opened the emperor's mind. Seeking quick results, he has forgotten his earlier learning.

sentences.zh: 尚法令則稱商鞅，言財利則背孟軻，鄙老成為因循，棄公論為流俗，異己者為不肖，合意者為賢人。

translations.literal: When law and ordinance are at issue he cites Shang Yang; when wealth and profit are at issue he turns his back on Mencius; he despises seasoned officials as hidebound, rejects public opinion as vulgar fashion, treats those who differ as worthless, and treats those who agree as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: When law and ordinance are at issue he cites Shang Yang; when wealth and profit are at issue he turns his back on Mencius. He despises seasoned officials as hidebound, dismisses public opinion as vulgar fashion, treats dissenters as worthless, and treats flatterers as worthy.

sentences.zh: 劉琦、錢顗等一言，便蒙降黜。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, Qian Yi, and others spoke a single word and at once suffered demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi, Qian Yi, and others spoke a single word and at once suffered demotion.

sentences.zh: 在廷之臣，方大半趨附。

translations.literal: Of the ministers at court, more than half were then rushing to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: More than half the ministers at court were then rushing to attach themselves to him.

sentences.zh: 陛下又從而驅之，其將何所不至。

translations.literal: Your Majesty again drives them on from above—where will this not reach?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty again drives them on from above—where will such a course not lead?

sentences.zh: 道遠者理當馴致，事大者不可速成，人材不可急求，積敝不可頓革。

translations.literal: The Way that is distant ought to be approached with gradual attainment; great affairs cannot be hastily completed; talent cannot be urgently sought; accumulated abuses cannot be suddenly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: The Way that is distant must be approached step by step. Great affairs cannot be rushed to completion. Talent cannot be hurriedly gathered. Accumulated abuses cannot be overturned at a stroke.

sentences.zh: 儻欲事功亟就，必為憸佞所乘，宜速還言者而退安石，答中外之望。」

translations.literal: If you wish achievement to come quickly, you will surely be ridden by the cunning and servile—Your Majesty should quickly restore the remonstrators and dismiss Anshi, to answer the hopes within and without."
translations.idiomatic: If you wish achievement to come quickly, you will surely be ridden by the cunning and servile. Your Majesty should quickly restore the remonstrators and dismiss Anshi, to answer the hopes of the empire within and without."

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 遂求罷諫職，改判國子監，去意愈確。

translations.literal: Chunren thereupon requested to be relieved of his remonstrance duties, was transferred to judge the Directorate of Education, and his resolve to leave grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren thereupon asked to be relieved of his remonstrance duties, was transferred to judge the Directorate of Education, and his resolve to leave office grew firmer.

sentences.zh: 執政使諭之曰：「毋輕去，已議除知制誥矣。」

translations.literal: Those in power sent someone to instruct him: "Do not leave lightly—you have already been slated for appointment as drafting attendant."
translations.idiomatic: Those in power sent someone to tell him: "Do not leave lightly—you have already been slated for appointment as drafting attendant.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「此言何為至於我哉，言不用，萬鐘非所顧也。」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Why should such words be spoken to me? If my words are not heeded, even ten thousand piculs of salary are not what I would regard.
