translations.idiomatic: Chunren replied, "Why should such words be spoken to me? If my counsel goes unheeded, even the highest salary is nothing I would covet."

sentences.zh: 其所上章疏，語多激切。

translations.literal: In the memorials he submitted, the language was often forceful and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: The memorials he submitted were often forceful and cutting in tone.

sentences.zh: 神宗悉不付外，純仁盡錄申中書，安石大怒，乞加重貶。

translations.literal: The emperor did not release any of them to the outside; Chunren copied them all and forwarded them to the Secretariat-Chancellery. Anshi was greatly angered and requested a heavier demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not release any of them outside the palace. Chunren copied them all and forwarded them to the Secretariat-Chancellery. Anshi was furious and asked that Chunren be more heavily punished.

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「彼無罪，姑與一善地。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He is without guilt—for the present give him a good post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is without guilt. For the present give him a good post."

sentences.zh: 命知河中府，徙成都路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as Prefect of Hezhong Prefecture and transferred to Transport Commissioner of the Chengdu route.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Hezhong and transferred to transport commissioner of the Chengdu route.

sentences.zh: 以新法不便，戒州縣未得遽行。

translations.literal: Because the new laws were inconvenient, he instructed the prefectures and counties not to implement them hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the new laws burdensome, he instructed the prefectures and counties not to implement them hastily.

sentences.zh: 安石怒純仁沮格，因讒者遣使欲捃摭私事，不能得。

translations.literal: Anshi was angry that Chunren was obstructing implementation and, through slanderers, dispatched an envoy intending to gather evidence of private wrongdoing, but none could be found.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was angry that Chunren was obstructing implementation and, through slanderers, dispatched an envoy to gather evidence of private wrongdoing, but none could be found.

sentences.zh: 使者以他事鞭傷傳言者，屬官喜謂純仁曰：「此一事足以塞其謗，請聞於朝。」

translations.literal: The envoy whipped and injured a messenger who was passing on word; a subordinate official rejoiced and said to Chunren: "This one matter is enough to block their slander—please report it to the court."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy whipped and injured a courier who was passing on word. A subordinate rejoiced and told Chunren: "This one matter is enough to block their slander—please report it to the court."

sentences.zh: 純仁既不奏使者之過，亦不折言者之非。

translations.literal: Chunren neither memorialized the envoy's fault nor rebuked the messenger's error.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren neither memorialized the envoy's fault nor rebuked the courier's error.

sentences.zh: 後竟坐失察僚佐燕游，左遷知和州，徙邢州。

translations.literal: Later he was finally punished for failing to supervise subordinates who feasted and went sightseeing; he was demoted to Prefect of He Prefecture and transferred to Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was punished for failing to supervise subordinates who feasted and went sightseeing; he was demoted to prefect of He and transferred to Xing.

sentences.zh: 未至，加直龍圖閣、知慶州。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, he was further made Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images and Prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up his new post, he was further made Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images and prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 過闕入對，神宗曰：「卿父在慶著威名，今可謂世職。

translations.literal: Passing through the capital to answer the emperor's summons, Emperor Shenzong said: "Your father won great renown at Qing; this may be called a hereditary post.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the capital to answer the emperor's summons, Shenzong said, "Your father won great renown at Qing. This may be called a hereditary post.

sentences.zh: 卿隨父既久，兵法必精，邊事必熟。」

translations.literal: You have long followed your father; your knowledge of military methods must be refined and your knowledge of frontier affairs must be thorough."
translations.idiomatic: You have long followed your father. Your knowledge of military methods must be refined and your knowledge of frontier affairs must be thorough."

sentences.zh: 純仁揣神宗有功名心，即對曰：「臣儒家，未嘗學兵，先臣守邊時，臣尚幼，不復記憶，且今日事勢宜有不同。

translations.literal: Chunren, sensing that the emperor had a mind for achievement and glory, immediately replied: "Your servant is a Confucian and has never studied warfare; when my late father held the frontier, I was still young and no longer remember. Moreover, the situation today ought to differ.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren, sensing that the emperor hungered for military glory, replied at once: "I am a Confucian and have never studied warfare. When my late father held the frontier I was still young and remember little. Moreover, the situation today ought to be different.

sentences.zh: 陛下使臣繕治城壘，愛養百姓，不敢辭；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty assigns me to repair city walls and cherish the people, I dare not decline;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty assigns me to repair the fortifications and care for the people, I dare not decline.

sentences.zh: 若開拓侵攘，願別謀帥臣。」

translations.literal: but if you wish to open new campaigns of aggression and encroachment, I pray that another commander be chosen."
translations.idiomatic: But if you wish to open new campaigns of aggression and encroachment, I pray that another commander be chosen."

sentences.zh: 神宗曰：「卿之才何所不能，顧不肯為朕悉心爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What is there that your talent cannot do? You simply will not exert yourself wholeheartedly for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What is there that your talent cannot accomplish? You simply refuse to exert yourself wholeheartedly for me."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: Chunren then departed.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren then departed for his post.

sentences.zh: 秦中方饑，擅發常平粟振貸。

translations.literal: Famine was then raging in Shaanxi; he on his own authority released grain from the ever-normal granaries for relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: Famine was then raging in Shaanxi. On his own authority Chunren released grain from the ever-normal granaries for relief loans.

sentences.zh: 僚屬請奏而須報，純仁曰：「報至無及矣，吾當獨任其責。」

translations.literal: His staff asked that he memorialize and await reply; Chunren said: "By the time a reply arrives it will be too late—I alone will bear the responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: His staff asked that he memorialize and await imperial reply. Chunren said, "By the time a reply arrives it will be too late. I alone will bear the responsibility."

sentences.zh: 或謗其所全活不實，詔遣使按視。

translations.literal: Some slandered him, saying the number he had saved was not true; an edict dispatched an envoy to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Some slandered him, claiming the number of lives he had saved was false. An edict dispatched an envoy to investigate.

sentences.zh: 會秋大稔，民歡曰：「公實活我，忍累公邪？」

translations.literal: When autumn brought a great harvest, the people rejoiced and said: "The governor truly saved our lives—how can we bear to bring trouble upon him?"
translations.idiomatic: When autumn brought a great harvest, the people rejoiced and said, "The governor truly saved our lives—how can we bear to bring trouble upon him?"

sentences.zh: 晝夜爭輸還之。

translations.literal: Day and night they competed to repay what they had borrowed.
translations.idiomatic: Day and night they competed to repay what they had borrowed.

sentences.zh: 使者至，已無所負。

translations.literal: When the envoy arrived, nothing remained unpaid.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy arrived, nothing remained unpaid.

sentences.zh: 邠、甯間有叢塚，使者曰：「全活不實之罪，於此得矣。」

translations.literal: Between Bin and Ning there were clusters of burial mounds; the envoy said: "The crime of falsely claiming lives saved is proved here.
translations.idiomatic: Between Bin and Ning there were clusters of burial mounds. The envoy said, "The crime of falsely claiming lives saved is proved here."

sentences.zh: 發塚籍骸上之。

translations.literal: He opened the mounds and registered the bones, reporting them upward.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the mounds, counted the bones, and reported them upward.

sentences.zh: 詔本路監司窮治，乃前帥楚建中所封也。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the circuit supervisory officials to investigate thoroughly; it turned out to be the work of the former commander Chu Jianzhong, who had sealed them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the circuit supervisory officials to investigate thoroughly. The mounds turned out to have been sealed by the former commander Chu Jianzhong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷治建中罪，純仁上疏言：「建中守法，申請間不免有殍死者，已坐罪罷去。

translations.literal: The court punished Jianzhong; Chunren submitted a memorial saying: "Jianzhong observed the law, and in the interval of his application there were unavoidably some who died of starvation; he was already punished and removed.
translations.idiomatic: The court punished Jianzhong. Chunren submitted a memorial: "Jianzhong observed the law, and while his requests were pending some unavoidably died of starvation. He was already punished and removed.

sentences.zh: 今緣按臣而及建中，是一罪再刑也。」

translations.literal: Now, because of the investigation of this minister, Jianzhong is implicated—this is punishing one crime twice.
translations.idiomatic: Now, because of the investigation directed at me, Jianzhong is implicated again. That is punishing one crime twice."

sentences.zh: 建中猶贖銅三十斤。

translations.literal: Jianzhong was nevertheless fined thirty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Jianzhong was nevertheless fined thirty jin of copper.

sentences.zh: 環州種古執熟羌為盜，流南方，過慶呼冤，純仁以屬吏，非盜也。

translations.literal: Zhong Gu of Huan Prefecture treated the Shufan Qiang as bandits and exiled them to the south; passing through Qing they cried out their innocence, and Chunren held that they were not bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Gu of Huan Prefecture treated the Shufan Qiang as bandits and exiled them to the south. Passing through Qing they cried out their innocence, and Chunren held that they were not bandits.

sentences.zh: 古避罪讕訟，詔御史治于寧州。

translations.literal: Gu, seeking to escape guilt, brought a false accusation; an edict ordered the censorate to try the case at Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gu, seeking to escape punishment, brought a false accusation. An edict ordered the censorate to try the case at Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 純仁就逮，民萬數遮馬涕泗，不得行，至有自投於河者。

translations.literal: When Chunren was taken into custody, tens of thousands of people blocked his horse in tears and would not let him go; some even threw themselves into the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunren was taken into custody, tens of thousands of people blocked his horse in tears and would not let him go. Some even threw themselves into the river.

sentences.zh: 獄成，古以誣告謫。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, Gu was demoted for false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was concluded, Gu was demoted for false accusation.

sentences.zh: 亦加純仁以他過，黜知信陽軍。

translations.literal: Chunren was also punished on another charge and dismissed to Prefect of Xinyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren was also punished on another charge and dismissed to prefect of Xinyang Army.

sentences.zh: 移齊州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 齊俗兇悍，人輕為盜劫。

translations.literal: The customs of Qi were fierce and violent; people lightly turned to robbery and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: The customs of Qi were fierce and violent, and people readily turned to robbery and plunder.

sentences.zh: 或謂：「此嚴治之猶不能戢，公一以寬，恐不勝其治矣。」

translations.literal: Some said: "Even severe governance cannot restrain this—if the governor applies leniency alone, I fear he will not be equal to governing it."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "Even harsh governance cannot restrain them. If the governor relies on leniency alone, I fear he will not be able to govern them."

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「寬出於性，若強以猛，則不能持久；

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Leniency comes from my nature; if I force myself to severity, I cannot sustain it;
translations.idiomatic: Chunren replied, "Leniency comes from my nature. If I force myself to severity, I cannot sustain it.

sentences.zh: 猛而不久，以治凶民，取玩之道也。」

translations.literal: severity that cannot last, when used to govern violent people, is the way to invite contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Severity that cannot last, when used to govern violent people, is the way to invite contempt."

sentences.zh: 有西司理院，系囚常滿，皆屠販盜竊而督償者。

translations.literal: There was a Western Judicial Review Office where prisoners were constantly full— all butchers, peddlers, thieves, and those detained to compel repayment.
translations.idiomatic: There was a Western Judicial Review Office where the cells were constantly full—mostly butchers, peddlers, thieves, and debtors held to compel repayment.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「此何不保外使輸納邪？」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Why not release them on bail to make payment outside?"
translations.idiomatic: Chunren asked, "Why not release them on bail to make payment outside?"

sentences.zh: 通判曰：「此釋之，復紊，官司往往待其以疾斃於獄中，是與民除害爾。」

translations.literal: The vice prefect said: "If these are released, they will again cause disorder; the office often waits for them to die of illness in prison— that is simply removing harm for the people."
translations.idiomatic: The vice prefect said, "If these are released, they will again cause disorder. The office often waits for them to die of illness in prison—that is simply removing harm for the people."

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「法不至死，以情殺之，豈理也邪？」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "When the law does not reach to death, to kill by sentiment—is that reasonable?"
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "When the law does not prescribe death, to kill by sentiment—is that reasonable?"

sentences.zh: 盡呼至庭下，訓使自新，即釋去。

translations.literal: He summoned them all to the hall, admonished them to reform themselves, and at once released them.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned them all to the hall, admonished them to reform themselves, and at once released them.

sentences.zh: 期歲，盜減比年大半。

translations.literal: Within a year, robbery decreased by more than half compared with recent years.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year, robbery decreased by more than half compared with recent years.

sentences.zh: 丐罷，提舉西京留司御史台。

translations.literal: He requested to be relieved of office and was given charge of the Western Capital Branch of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He requested to be relieved of office and was given charge of the Western Capital branch of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 時耆賢多在洛，純仁及司馬光，皆好客而家貧，相約為真率會，脫粟一飯，酒數行，洛中以為勝事。

translations.literal: At that time many elder worthies were in Luoyang; Chunren and Sima Guang were both fond of guests yet poor in means, and together they formed a Plain Fellowship, sharing a meal of husked millet and a few rounds of wine—a thing Luoyang regarded as a surpassing pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many elder worthies lived in Luoyang. Chunren and Sima Guang were both fond of guests yet poor in means. Together they formed a Plain Fellowship, sharing a meal of husked millet and a few rounds of wine—a custom Luoyang regarded as a surpassing pleasure.

sentences.zh: 復知河中，諸路閱保甲妨農，論救甚力。

translations.literal: He again served as Prefect of Hezhong and argued forcefully against the circuit-wide review of the baojia militia, which was harming agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as prefect of Hezhong and argued forcefully against the circuit-wide review of the baojia militia, which was harming agriculture.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍宋儋年暴死，純仁使子弟視喪，小殮，口鼻血出。

translations.literal: Song Danian, recording secretary, died suddenly; Chunren sent his sons to attend the funeral, and at the minor encoffinement blood issued from the nose and mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Song Danian, the recording secretary, died suddenly. Chunren sent his sons to attend the funeral, and at the minor encoffinement blood issued from the nose and mouth.

sentences.zh: 純仁疑其非命，按得其妾與小吏奸，因會，寘毒鱉肉中。

translations.literal: Chunren suspected death by violence; investigation revealed that his concubine had committed adultery with a petty clerk and, at a gathering, placed poison in turtle meat.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren suspected foul play. Investigation revealed that Danian's concubine had committed adultery with a petty clerk and, at a gathering, placed poison in turtle meat.

sentences.zh: 純仁問食肉在第幾巡，曰：「豈有既中毒而尚能終席者乎？」

translations.literal: Chunren asked in which round of the feast the meat had been eaten, saying: "How could one who had already been poisoned still finish the banquet?"
translations.idiomatic: Chunren asked in which round of the feast the meat had been eaten, saying, "How could one who had already been poisoned still finish the banquet?"

sentences.zh: 再訊之，則儋年素不食鱉，其曰毒鱉肉者，蓋妾與吏欲為變獄張本，以逃死爾。

translations.literal: On further questioning, it turned out that Danian had never eaten turtle; their claim of poisoned turtle meat was simply the concubine and the clerk laying groundwork to overturn the case and escape death.
translations.idiomatic: On further questioning it turned out that Danian had never eaten turtle. Their claim of poisoned turtle meat was simply the concubine and the clerk laying groundwork to overturn the case and escape death.

sentences.zh: 實儋年醉歸，毒於酒而殺之。

translations.literal: In fact Danian returned home drunk and was killed by poison placed in wine.
translations.idiomatic: In fact Danian returned home drunk and was killed by poison placed in wine.

sentences.zh: 遂正其罪。

translations.literal: Their guilt was thereupon established.
translations.idiomatic: Their guilt was thereupon established.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，復直龍圖閣、知慶州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Chunren was again made Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images and Prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne, Chunren was again made Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Images and prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 召為右諫議大夫，以親嫌辭，改天章閣待制兼侍講，除給事中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Right Remonstrance Grandee but declined on account of kinship obligations; he was changed to Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, concurrently Court Lecturer, and appointed Chief of the Drafting Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Right Remonstrance Grandee but declined on account of kinship obligations. He was instead made Attendant Drafting Academician of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns, concurrently court lecturer, and appointed chief of the drafting office.

sentences.zh: 時宣仁後垂簾，司馬光為政，將盡改熙甯、元豐法度。

translations.literal: At that time the Empress Dowager Xuanren held court from behind the curtain and Sima Guang held power, intending to overturn entirely the laws and institutions of the Xining and Yuanfeng reigns.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Xuanren held court from behind the curtain and Sima Guang held power, intending to overturn entirely the laws and institutions of the Xining and Yuanfeng reigns.

sentences.zh: 純仁謂光：「去其太甚者可也。

translations.literal: Chunren said to Guang: "Removing what is excessive would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren told Guang, "Removing what is excessive would suffice.

sentences.zh: 差役一事，尤當熟講而緩行，不然，滋為民病。

translations.literal: The matter of the hired-service system above all ought to be carefully debated and slowly implemented; otherwise it will increasingly become a burden on the people.
translations.idiomatic: The hired-service system, above all, ought to be carefully debated and slowly implemented. Otherwise it will increasingly become a burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 願公虛心以延眾論，不必謀自己出；

translations.literal: I pray that you open your mind to extend to the opinions of the multitude—you need not insist that every plan come from yourself;
translations.idiomatic: I pray that you open your mind to the opinions of the multitude and need not insist that every plan come from yourself.

sentences.zh: 謀自己出，則諂諛得乘間迎合矣。

translations.literal: if plans come from yourself, then flatterers will seize the interval to suit and agree.
translations.idiomatic: If plans must come from yourself, flatterers will seize the chance to suit and agree with you.

sentences.zh: 役議或難回，則可先行之一路，以觀其究竟。」

translations.literal: If debate over the service system is hard to turn back, you may first implement it on one route and observe the outcome."
translations.idiomatic: If debate over the service system proves hard to reverse, you may first implement it on one circuit and observe the outcome."

sentences.zh: 光不從，持之益豎。

translations.literal: Guang did not listen and held all the more firmly to his course.
translations.idiomatic: Guang did not listen and held all the more firmly to his course.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「是使人不得言爾。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "This is simply to keep people from speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "This is really just a way to keep people from speaking their minds.

sentences.zh: 若欲媚公以為容悅，何如少年合安石以速富貴哉。」

translations.literal: If I wished to flatter you for favor and pleasure, why not, as in my youth, have joined with Anshi to rise swiftly to wealth and rank?"
translations.idiomatic: If I wanted to curry your favor and please you, I might as well have done what I did in my youth—throw in my lot with Wang Anshi and hurry toward wealth and high office."

sentences.zh: 又云：「熙寧按問自首之法，既已行之，有司立文太深，四方死者視舊數倍，殆非先王寧失不經之意。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Xining law on interrogation and voluntary confession has already been put into practice, but the officials drafted the regulations too harshly. The dead in all directions are several times the former number—hardly in the spirit of the ancient kings' principle that it is better to let guilt go than to punish wrongly."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The Xining regulations on interrogation and voluntary confession are already in force, yet the agencies have written the rules far too severely. Deaths across the realm are now many times what they once were—hardly what the ancient kings meant when they said it is better to let the guilty escape than to punish the innocent."

sentences.zh: 純仁素與光同志，及臨事規正，類如此。

translations.literal: Chunren had long shared Guang's aims, yet when facing affairs he corrected them in this manner.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren had long been of one mind with Sima Guang, yet when matters came before him he corrected course in just this way.

sentences.zh: 初，種古因誣純仁停任。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhong Gu had caused Chunren to be suspended from office by making false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhong Gu had brought false charges against Chunren and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 至是，純仁薦為永興軍路鈐轄，又薦知隰州。

translations.literal: Now Chunren recommended him as military intendant of Yongxing Circuit and later as prefect of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Chunren recommended him as military intendant on the Yongxing Circuit route and later as prefect of Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 每自咎曰：「先人與種氏上世有契義，純仁不肖，為其子孫所訟，甯論曲直哉。」

translations.literal: He often blamed himself, saying: "Our forebear and the Zhong clan's ancestors had a bond of loyalty. Chunren is unworthy—having been sued by their descendants, how could I argue right and wrong?"
translations.idiomatic: He often reproached himself, saying, "Our ancestor and the Zhong family's forebears had a covenant of loyalty. Chunren is unworthy—sued by their descendants, how could I stand on right and wrong?"

sentences.zh: 元祐初，進吏部尚書，數日，同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanyou era, he was promoted to Minister of Personnel; within days he became Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou reign he was promoted to Minister of Personnel, and within a few days was made Associate Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，純仁與議西夏，請罷兵棄地，使歸所掠漢人，執政持之未決。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chunren had joined in deliberations on Western Xia, proposing to cease hostilities and abandon territory and to have them return Han people they had seized; the chief ministers withheld decision.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chunren had taken part in deliberations on Western Xia, urging that fighting be stopped, territory abandoned, and captured Han subjects returned; the chief ministers had held back without deciding.

sentences.zh: 至是，乃申前議，又請歸一漢人予十縑。

translations.literal: Now he renewed the earlier proposal and further asked that ten bolts of silk be given for each Han person returned.
translations.idiomatic: Now he pressed the earlier proposal again and further asked that ten bolts of silk be paid for each Han person returned.

sentences.zh: 事皆施行。

translations.literal: All these measures were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: All of these measures were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 邊俘鬼章以獻，純仁請誅之塞上，以謝邊人，不聽。

translations.literal: A border captive, Gui Zhang, was presented; Chunren asked that he be executed on the frontier to satisfy the border people, but the request was refused.
translations.idiomatic: The border captive Gui Zhang was brought forward as tribute. Chunren asked that he be executed on the frontier as satisfaction to the border people, but the court would not agree.

sentences.zh: 議者欲致其子，收河南故地，故赦不殺。

translations.literal: Deliberators wished to bring his son and recover former Henan territory, so he was spared by amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Those debating the matter hoped to summon his son and recover the old Henan lands, and so he was spared rather than executed.

sentences.zh: 後又欲官之，純仁復固爭，然鬼章子卒不至。

translations.literal: Later they again wished to grant him office; Chunren again argued firmly against it, yet Gui Zhang's son never came.
translations.idiomatic: Later they again wanted to give him an official post; Chunren again argued strenuously against it, but Gui Zhang's son never arrived.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 純仁在位，務以博大開上意，忠篤革士風。

translations.literal: In office, Chunren strove to broaden the emperor's mind with magnanimity and to reform the temperament of scholars through sincerity and loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: While in power, Chunren worked to open the emperor's mind through breadth of spirit and to reform the moral tone of the scholar-official class through sincerity and steadfast loyalty.

sentences.zh: 章惇得罪去，朝廷以其父老，欲畀便郡，既而中止。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun left office after incurring guilt; the court, considering his father was old, wished to give him an easy prefecture but then dropped the idea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun fell from grace and left office. The court, noting that his father was elderly, at first wanted to give him a comfortable prefecture, then abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 純仁請置往咎而念其私情。

translations.literal: Chunren asked that past offenses be set aside and private feeling be considered.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren asked that past wrongs be set aside and private feeling be taken into account.

sentences.zh: 鄧綰帥淮東，言者斥之不已。

translations.literal: Deng Wan commanded Huaidong, and critics denounced him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan was in command on the Huaidong circuit, and critics attacked him without letup.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「臣嘗為綰誣奏坐黜，今日所陳為綰也，左降不宜錄人之過太深。」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Your subject was once dismissed on Wan's false memorial. What I say today is on Wan's behalf—demotion should not record a man's faults too deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Your subject was once removed from office on the strength of Wan's false memorial. What I say today is on Wan's behalf—a demotion should not dwell too deeply on a man's past faults."

sentences.zh: 宣仁後嘉納。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 因下詔：「前日希合附會之人，一無所問。」

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued: "Those who yesterday curried favor and clung to factions shall not be questioned at all."
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: "Those who yesterday fawned and attached themselves to factions are not to be questioned at all."

sentences.zh: 學士蘇軾以發策問為言者所攻，韓維無名罷門下侍郎補外。

translations.literal: Academician Su Shi was assailed by critics for setting examination questions; Han Wei, without stated cause, was removed as Vice Director of the Chancellery and sent outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Su Shi came under attack from critics for the palace examination questions he had set; Han Wei, with no reason given, was removed as Vice Director of the Chancellery and sent to a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 純仁奏軾無罪，維盡心國家，不可因譖黜官。

translations.literal: Chunren memorialized that Shi was innocent and that Wei served the state with all his heart—they should not be dismissed on slander.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren memorialized that Su Shi was innocent and that Han Wei had served the state with all his heart—they should not be dismissed on the basis of slander.

sentences.zh: 及王覿言事忤旨，純仁慮朋黨將熾，與文彥博、呂公著辨於簾前，未解。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhi spoke on affairs and displeased the throne, Chunren feared factions would swell; with Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongzhu he argued before the curtain, without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhi spoke on state affairs and offended the throne, Chunren feared that factionalism would flare up. With Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongzhu he argued the matter before the regent's curtain, but no conclusion was reached.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「朝臣本無黨，但善惡邪正，各以類分。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Court ministers form no factions by nature; good and evil, upright and corrupt, simply group by kind.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Court ministers are not factions by nature; good and evil, the upright and the corrupt, simply sort themselves by kind.

sentences.zh: 彥博、公著皆累朝舊人，豈容雷同罔上。

translations.literal: Yanbo and Gongzhu are veterans of many reigns—how could they band together to deceive their superiors?
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and Gongzhu are men of many reigns—how could they possibly band together to deceive their superiors?

sentences.zh: 昔先臣與韓琦、富弼同慶曆柄任，各舉所知，常時飛語指為朋黨，三人相繼補外，造謗者公相慶曰一綱打盡，此事未遠，願陛下戒之。」

translations.literal: In the past my late father served with Han Qi and Fu Bi in Qingli, each recommending men he knew; at the time idle talk called them a faction. The three were sent outside in succession, and the slanderers openly rejoiced that the whole net had been pulled in. This is not long ago—Your Majesty, I beg you to take warning."
translations.idiomatic: In the past my late father served with Han Qi and Fu Bi during the Qingli reforms, each recommending men he knew; at the time loose talk called them a faction. The three were sent out of the capital one after another, and the slanderers openly rejoiced that the whole catch had been hauled in with one pull of the net. That is not long ago—Your Majesty, I beg you to take warning from it."

sentences.zh: 因極言前世朋黨之禍，並錄歐陽修《朋黨論》以進。

translations.literal: He then spoke at length on the calamities of factions in earlier ages and submitted a copy of Ouyang Xiu's "Essay on Factions."
translations.idiomatic: He then spoke at length on the disasters wrought by factions in earlier ages and submitted a copy of Ouyang Xiu's "Essay on Factions."

sentences.zh: 知漢陽軍吳處厚傅致蔡確安州《車蓋亭詩》，以為謗宣仁后，上之。

translations.literal: Wu Chuhou, military prefect of Hanyang, transmitted by report Cai Que's "Chariot Pavilion" poems from An Prefecture, claiming they slandered Empress Dowager Xuanren, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chuhou, prefect of Hanyang, forwarded by report Cai Que's "Chariot Pavilion" poems from An Prefecture, claiming they slandered Empress Dowager Xuanren, and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 諫官欲寘於典憲，執政右其說，唯純仁與左丞王存以為不可。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials wished to punish under the penal code; the chief ministers supported them—only Chunren and Left Vice Director Wang Cun thought it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials wanted to punish Cai Que under the penal code; the chief ministers sided with them—only Chunren and Left Vice Director Wang Cun held that this should not be done.

sentences.zh: 爭之未定，聞太師文彥博欲貶於嶺嶠，純仁謂左相呂大防曰：「此路自乾興以來，荊棘近七十年，吾輩開之，恐自不免。」

translations.literal: While debate was unsettled, he heard Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo wished to banish Que to the Ling mountains. Chunren said to Left Chancellor Lü Dafang: "Since Qianxing this path has been choked with thorns for nearly seventy years. If we open it, I fear we ourselves will not escape it."
translations.idiomatic: While the debate remained unresolved, he heard that Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo wanted to banish Que to the Lingnan frontier. Chunren said to Left Chancellor Lü Dafang, "Since the Qianxing era this road has been overgrown with thorns for nearly seventy years. If we open it, I fear we ourselves will not escape traveling it."

sentences.zh: 大防遂不敢言。

translations.literal: Dafang then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang then no longer dared to speak.

sentences.zh: 及確新州命下，純仁于宣仁后簾前言：「聖朝宜務寬厚，不可以語言文字之間曖昧不明之過，誅竄大臣。

translations.literal: When Que's assignment to Xin Prefecture was issued, Chunren spoke before Empress Dowager Xuanren's curtain: "Our sage dynasty should strive for generosity. One must not banish and cast out great ministers over vague faults in words and writings.
translations.idiomatic: When the order sending Que to Xin Prefecture was issued, Chunren spoke before Empress Dowager Xuanren's curtain: "Our sage dynasty should strive for generosity. One must not banish and cast out great ministers over vague and uncertain faults in words and writing.

sentences.zh: 今舉動宜與將來為法，此事甚不可開端也。

translations.literal: Present conduct should become the model for the future—this matter must not be given a beginning.
translations.idiomatic: What we do now should become the standard for the future—this is a door that must not be opened.

sentences.zh: 且以重刑除惡，如以猛藥治病，其過也，不能無損焉。」

translations.literal: Moreover, to remove evil with heavy punishments is like treating illness with fierce drugs—even when justified, harm cannot be entirely avoided."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, to root out evil with heavy punishments is like treating disease with fierce drugs—even when the remedy is called for, some harm cannot be avoided."

sentences.zh: 又與王存諫于哲宗，退而上疏，其略云：「蓋如父母之有逆子，雖天地鬼神不能容貸，父子至親，主於恕而已。

translations.literal: With Wang Cun he remonstrated before Emperor Zhezong; on retiring he submitted a memorial whose gist read: "It is like parents with a rebellious son—though Heaven and earth and spirits cannot pardon him, between father and son, utmost kinship, what should prevail is forgiveness alone.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Wang Cun he remonstrated before Emperor Zhezong, and on retiring submitted a memorial whose gist was: "It is like parents with a rebellious son—though Heaven and earth and the spirits cannot pardon him, between father and son, who are bound by the closest kinship, what should prevail is forgiveness alone.

sentences.zh: 若處之必死之地，則恐傷恩。」

translations.literal: If he is placed in ground where death is certain, I fear affection will be wounded."
translations.idiomatic: If he is placed in circumstances where death is all but certain, I fear the bond of affection will be wounded."

sentences.zh: 確卒貶新州。

translations.literal: In the end Que was demoted to Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Cai Que was demoted to Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大防奏確黨人甚盛，不可不問。

translations.literal: Dafang memorialized that Que's faction was very large and could not go uninvestigated.
translations.idiomatic: Dafang memorialized that Cai Que's faction was very large and could not be left uninvestigated.

sentences.zh: 純仁面諫朋黨難辨，恐誤及善人。

translations.literal: Chunren remonstrated in person that factions are hard to distinguish and good men might be harmed by mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren remonstrated in person that factions are hard to distinguish and that good men might be swept up by mistake.

sentences.zh: 遂上疏曰：「朋黨之起，蓋因趣向異同，同我者謂之正人，異我者疑為邪黨。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Factions arise because inclinations differ—those who agree with me are called upright; those who differ are suspected as an evil faction.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Factions arise because people's inclinations differ—those who agree with me are called upright men; those who differ are suspected of forming an evil faction.

sentences.zh: 既惡其異我，則逆耳之言難至；

translations.literal: Once one hates those who differ, unwelcome words hardly arrive;
translations.idiomatic: Once one hates those who differ, unwelcome words hardly reach one's ears;

sentences.zh: 既喜其同我，則迎合之佞日親。

translations.literal: once one delights in those who agree, flatterers who cater daily grow close.
translations.idiomatic: once one delights in those who agree, sycophants who cater to one grow closer day by day.

sentences.zh: 以至真偽莫知，賢愚倒置，國家之患，率由此也。

translations.literal: Truth and falsehood become unknown; worthy and foolish are reversed—the state's troubles mostly stem from this.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and falsehood become impossible to tell apart; the worthy and the foolish are reversed in rank—the state's troubles mostly spring from this.

sentences.zh: 至如王安石，正因喜同惡異，遂至黑白不分，至今風俗，猶以觀望為能，後來柄臣，固合永為商鑒。

translations.literal: Take Wang Anshi—precisely because he favored agreement and hated difference, black and white went undistinguished. To this day custom still treats watching and waiting as skill; later power-holders should take this as an everlasting lesson.
translations.idiomatic: Take Wang Anshi—precisely because he loved agreement and hated difference, black and white could no longer be distinguished. Even now the custom persists of treating watchful hesitation as a talent; later holders of power should forever take this as a warning.

sentences.zh: 今蔡確不必推治黨人，旁及枝葉。

translations.literal: Now with Cai Que there is no need to extend the investigation to his faction and reach the branches and leaves.
translations.idiomatic: In Cai Que's case there is no need to extend the investigation to his faction and reach out to every branch and leaf.

sentences.zh: 臣聞孔子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。』

translations.literal: I have heard Confucius say: 'Raise the upright and set them above the crooked, and the crooked will become straight.'
translations.idiomatic: I have heard Confucius say, "Raise the upright and set them above the crooked, and the crooked will become straight."

sentences.zh: 則是舉用正直，而可以化枉邪為善人，不仁者自當屏跡矣。

translations.literal: Thus by elevating the upright one can transform the crooked and evil into good men, and the unkind will naturally withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: That is to say, by elevating and employing the upright one can transform the crooked and evil into good men, and the unkind will naturally withdraw of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 何煩分辨黨人，或恐有傷仁化。」

translations.literal: Why trouble to sort out factions—perhaps for fear of harming humane governance?"
translations.idiomatic: Why go to the trouble of sorting out factions—unless one fears damaging the work of humane governance?"

sentences.zh: 司諫吳安詩、正言劉安世交章擊純仁黨確，純仁亦力求罷。

translations.literal: Supervising Remonstrator Wu Anshi and Rectifier Liu Anshi submitted successive memorials attacking Chunren for siding with Que; Chunren also strenuously sought dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Remonstrator Wu Anshi and Rectifier Liu Anshi submitted successive memorials attacking Chunren for siding with Cai Que; Chunren also pressed hard for his own dismissal.

sentences.zh: 明年，以觀文殿學士知潁昌府。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Magistrate of Yingchang Prefecture with the title Academician of the Hall for Exalted Literature.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made magistrate of Yingchang Prefecture with the title Academician of the Hall for Exalted Literature.

sentences.zh: 逾年，加大學士、知太原府。

translations.literal: A year later he received the higher academician title and governed Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was given the higher academician title and appointed magistrate of Taiyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其境土狹民眾，惜地不葬。

translations.literal: Its territory was narrow and population dense; people begrudged land for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The territory was cramped and the population dense; people begrudged land for burial.

sentences.zh: 純仁遣僚屬收無主燼骨，別男女異穴，葬者三千餘。

translations.literal: Chunren sent subordinates to gather ownerless charred bones, separated men and women into different graves, and buried more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren sent his staff to gather ownerless charred bones, separated men and women into different graves, and buried more than three thousand bodies.

sentences.zh: 又推之一路，葬以萬數計。

translations.literal: He extended this through the circuit; burials ran into the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He extended the practice across the circuit, and burials ran into the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 夏人犯境，朝廷欲罪將吏。

translations.literal: When Tangut raiders crossed the border, the court wished to punish officers.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangut raiders crossed the border, the court wanted to punish the frontier officers.

sentences.zh: 純仁自引咎求貶。

translations.literal: Chunren took blame upon himself and sought demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren took the blame upon himself and asked to be demoted.

sentences.zh: 秋，有詔貶官一等，徙河南府，再徙潁昌。

translations.literal: In autumn an edict demoted him one rank; he was transferred to Henan Prefecture, then again to Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn an edict demoted him one rank; he was transferred to Henan Prefecture, then again to Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 召還，復拜右僕射。

translations.literal: Summoned back, he was again appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned back to court, he was again appointed Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 因入謝，宣仁后簾中諭曰：「或謂卿必先引用王覿、彭汝礪，卿宜與呂大防一心。」

translations.literal: On entering to give thanks, Empress Dowager Xuanren instructed from behind the curtain: "Some say you will first bring in Wang Zhi and Peng Rulin—you should be of one mind with Lü Dafang."
translations.idiomatic: When he entered to give thanks, Empress Dowager Xuanren instructed him from behind the curtain: "Some say you will first bring in Wang Zhi and Peng Rulin—you should be of one mind with Lü Dafang."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此二人實有士望，臣終不敢保位蔽賢，望陛下加察。」

translations.literal: He replied: "These two men truly command scholarly respect. Your subject would never cling to office and hide talent—I beg Your Majesty to examine this closely."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "These two men truly enjoy scholarly esteem. Your subject would never hold on to office and conceal talent—I beg Your Majesty to look into this closely."

sentences.zh: 純仁將再入也，楊畏不悅，嘗有言，純仁不知。

translations.literal: When Chunren was about to enter office again, Yang Wei was displeased and had spoken against it—Chunren did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunren was about to return to office, Yang Wei was displeased and had spoken against him—Chunren did not know this.

sentences.zh: 至是，大防約畏為助，欲引為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Now Dafang enlisted Wei as ally and wished to make him Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Dafang enlisted Wei as an ally and wanted to appoint him Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「諫官當用正人，畏不可用。」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Remonstrance officials should be upright men—Wei is not fit."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Remonstrance officials should be upright men—Wei is not fit for the post."

sentences.zh: 大防曰：「豈以畏嘗言公邪？」

translations.literal: Dafang said: "Is it because Wei once spoke against you?"
translations.idiomatic: Dafang said, "Is it because Wei once spoke against you?"

sentences.zh: 純仁始知之。

translations.literal: Then Chunren learned of it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Chunren learn of it.

sentences.zh: 後畏叛大防，凡有以害大防者，無所不至。

translations.literal: Later Wei turned against Dafang; anything that could harm Dafang he did without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wei turned against Dafang; whatever might harm Dafang, he did without limit.

sentences.zh: 宣仁後寢疾，召純仁曰：「卿父仲淹，可謂忠臣。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren fell ill and summoned Chunren: "Your father Zhongyan was a true loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren fell ill and summoned Chunren, saying, "Your father Zhongyan was a true loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 在明肅皇后垂簾時，唯勸明肅盡母道；

translations.literal: During Empress Ming Su's regency he only urged her to fulfill a mother's way;
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Ming Su's regency he urged her only to fulfill a mother's duty;

sentences.zh: 明肅上賓，唯勸仁宗盡子道。

translations.literal: when Ming Su departed this life he only urged Renzong to fulfill a son's way.
translations.idiomatic: when Ming Su passed away he urged Renzong only to fulfill a son's duty.

sentences.zh: 卿當似之。」

translations.literal: You should be like him."
translations.idiomatic: You should be like him."

sentences.zh: 純仁泣曰：「敢不盡忠。

translations.literal: Chunren wept and said: "How would I dare not give my full loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Chunren wept and said, "How could I dare not give my full loyalty?

sentences.zh: 宣仁后崩，哲宗親政，純仁乞避位。

translations.literal: After Empress Dowager Xuanren died, Zhezong took personal rule; Chunren asked to yield his place.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Xuanren died, Emperor Zhezong took personal rule, and Chunren asked to step aside.

sentences.zh: 哲宗語呂大防曰：「純仁有時望，不宜去，可為朕留之。」

translations.literal: Zhezong told Lü Dafang: "Chunren enjoys public esteem—he should not leave. Keep him for Us."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong told Lü Dafang, "Chunren enjoys public esteem—he should not leave. Keep him for me."

sentences.zh: 且趣入見，問：「先朝行青苗法如何？」

translations.literal: He hurried him in for audience and asked: "How was the green sprouts law under the previous reign?"
translations.idiomatic: He hurried Chunren in for an audience and asked, "How was the green sprouts law under the previous reign?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「先帝愛民之意本深，但王安石立法過甚，激以賞罰，故官吏急切，以致害民。」

translations.literal: He answered: "The late emperor's intent to love the people was deep, but Wang Anshi's legislation went too far, spurred by rewards and punishments, so officials acted urgently and harmed the people."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The late emperor's intent to love the people was deep, but Wang Anshi's legislation went too far and was driven by rewards and punishments, so officials acted with excessive urgency and ended up harming the people."

sentences.zh: 退而上疏，其要以為「青苗非所當行，行之終不免擾民也」。

translations.literal: On retiring he submitted a memorial whose gist was that green sprouts should not be implemented—if implemented, disturbance of the people could not ultimately be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: On retiring he submitted a memorial whose gist was that the green sprouts policy ought not to be carried out—that if it were, disturbance of the people could not ultimately be avoided.

sentences.zh: 是時，用二三大臣，皆從中出，侍從、臺諫官，亦多不由進擬。

translations.literal: At this time appointments of two or three great ministers all came from the inner court; attendants and censorial remonstrators also often bypassed normal nomination.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the appointment of two or three great ministers all came from the inner court; attendants and censorial remonstrators also often bypassed the usual nomination process.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「陛下初親政，四方拭目以觀，天下治亂，實本於此。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Your Majesty has just begun personal rule; the four quarters watch with open eyes—order and disorder under Heaven truly hinge on this.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Your Majesty has only just begun to rule in person; the four quarters watch with open eyes—the order or disorder of the realm truly hinges on this.

sentences.zh: 舜舉皋陶，湯舉伊尹，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Shun raised Gao Yao, Tang raised Yi Yin—the unkind kept their distance.
translations.idiomatic: Shun raised Gao Yao, Tang raised Yi Yin—and the unkind kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 縱未能如古人，亦須極天下之選。」

translations.literal: Even if we cannot match the ancients, we must still choose from the finest under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we cannot match the ancients, we must still choose from the finest talent under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 又群小力排宣仁后垂簾時事，純仁奏曰：「太皇保佑聖躬，功烈誠心，幽明共監，議者不恤國事，一何薄哉。」

translations.literal: Again petty men vigorously attacked affairs of Empress Dowager Xuanren's regency. Chunren memorialized: "The Grand Empress protected the sacred person—merit, loyalty, and sincere heart witnessed by shade and light alike. The critics care nothing for state affairs—how shallow!"
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile petty men vigorously attacked the affairs of Empress Dowager Xuanren's regency. Chunren memorialized, "The Grand Empress protected the sacred person—her merit, loyalty, and sincere heart were witnessed by the living and the dead alike. The critics care nothing for the affairs of state—how shallow!"

sentences.zh: 遂以仁宗禁言明肅垂簾事詔書上之。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted the edict by which Renzong forbade discussion of Ming Su's regency.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon submitted the edict by which Emperor Renzong had forbidden discussion of Empress Ming Su's regency.

sentences.zh: 曰：「望陛下稽仿而行，以戒薄俗。」

translations.literal: saying: "Your Majesty, I hope you will examine and follow it to warn against shallow custom."
translations.idiomatic: saying, "Your Majesty, I hope you will examine it and follow its example as a warning against shallow custom."

sentences.zh: 蘇轍論殿試策問，引漢昭變武帝法度事。

translations.literal: Su Zhe, discussing palace examination questions, cited Emperor Zhao of Han changing Emperor Wu's institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe, in discussing the palace examination questions, cited Emperor Zhao of Han changing the institutions of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 哲宗震怒曰：「安得以漢武比先帝？」

translations.literal: Zhezong erupted: "How dare you compare Emperor Wu to the late emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong erupted in anger: "How dare you compare Emperor Wu to the late emperor?"

sentences.zh: 轍下殿待罪，眾不敢仰視。

translations.literal: Zhe left the hall awaiting punishment; none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe left the hall to await punishment; no one dared raise his eyes.

sentences.zh: 純仁從容言：「武帝雄才大略，史無貶辭。

translations.literal: Chunren said calmly: "Emperor Wu was heroic in talent and grand in design—the histories carry no word of blame.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said calmly, "Emperor Wu was heroic in talent and grand in design—the histories carry no word of blame against him.

sentences.zh: 轍以比先帝，非謗也。

translations.literal: Zhe's comparison with the late emperor is not slander.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe's comparison with the late emperor is not slander.

sentences.zh: 陛下親事之始，進退大臣，不當如訶叱奴僕。」

translations.literal: At the start of Your Majesty's personal governance, advancing or dismissing great ministers should not be like scolding servants."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Your Majesty's personal rule, advancing or dismissing great ministers should not be like scolding servants."

sentences.zh: 右丞鄧潤甫越次曰：「先帝法度，為司馬光、蘇轍壞盡。」

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Deng Runfu interrupted: "The late emperor's institutions were ruined entirely by Sima Guang and Su Zhe."
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director Deng Runfu interrupted out of turn, "The late emperor's institutions were ruined entirely by Sima Guang and Su Zhe."

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「不然，法本無弊，弊則當改。」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Not so—law by nature has no flaw; when flawed, it should be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Not so—law by nature has no flaw; when a law proves flawed, it should be changed."

sentences.zh: 哲宗曰：「人謂秦皇、漢武。」

translations.literal: Zhezong said: "People speak of Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong said, "People speak of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han."

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「轍所論，事與時也，非人也。」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "What Zhe discussed was the matter and its time—not the man."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "What Su Zhe discussed was the matter and its time—not the man himself."

sentences.zh: 哲宗為之少霽。

translations.literal: Zhezong's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhezong's anger eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 轍平日與純仁多異，至是乃服謝純仁曰：「公佛地位中人也。」

translations.literal: Zhe had often differed from Chunren, but now submitted and thanked him: "Sir, you are a man midway to Buddhahood."
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe had often differed from Chunren, but now submitted and thanked him, saying, "Sir, you are a man midway to Buddhahood."

sentences.zh: 轍竟落職知汝州。

translations.literal: Zhe was ultimately stripped of office and made prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe was ultimately stripped of office and made prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 全台言蘇軾行呂惠卿告詞，訕謗先帝，黜知英州。

translations.literal: The full censoriate said Su Shi, when drafting Lü Huiqing's appointment text, mocked the late emperor; he was demoted to prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The full censoriate said that Su Shi, in drafting Lü Huiqing's appointment edict, had mocked the late emperor; he was demoted to prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 純仁上疏曰：「熙甯法度，皆惠卿附會王安石建議，不副先帝愛民求治之意。

translations.literal: Chunren submitted a memorial: "The Xining institutions were all proposals by Huiqing echoing Wang Anshi—they did not match the late emperor's intent to love the people and seek good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren submitted a memorial saying, "The Xining institutions were all proposals put forward by Lü Huiqing in echo of Wang Anshi—they did not match the late emperor's intent to love the people and seek good governance.

sentences.zh: 至垂簾之際，始用言者，特行貶竄，今已八年矣。

translations.literal: Only when the regency began were critics finally used to carry out demotions and banishments—and that was already eight years ago.
translations.idiomatic: It was only during the regency that critics were at last heeded and demotions and banishments were carried out—and that was already eight years ago.

sentences.zh: 言者多當時御史，何故畏避不即納忠，今乃有是奏，豈非觀望邪？」

translations.literal: Most of the critics were censors of that time—why did they fear to speak loyally then, and only now submit such memorials? Are they not simply watching which way the wind blows?"
translations.idiomatic: Most of those speaking now were censors at the time—why then did they shrink from offering loyal counsel immediately, and only now submit such memorials? Are they not simply watching which way the wind blows?"

sentences.zh: 御史來之邵言高士敦任成都鈐轄日不法事，及蘇轍所謫太近。

translations.literal: Censor Lai Zhi Shao spoke of unlawful acts by Gao Shidun when he served as military intendant of Chengdu, and that Su Zhe's place of exile was too near.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lai Zhi Shao reported unlawful acts by Gao Shidun during his service as military intendant of Chengdu, and argued that Su Zhe's place of exile was too close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 純仁言：「之邵為成都監司，士敦有犯，自當按發。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Zhi Shao was a supervisory official in Chengdu; if Shidun had committed offenses, he should have investigated them then.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Zhi Shao was a supervisory official in Chengdu; if Shidun had committed offenses, he should have investigated and reported them at the time.

sentences.zh: 轍與政累年，之邵已作御史，亦無糾正，今乃繼有二奏，其情可知。」

translations.literal: Zhe had held office for many years; Zhi Shao had already become a censor yet made no correction—now he submits two memorials in succession; his motive is plain."
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhe had held office for many years; Zhi Shao had already become a censor yet made no correction—now he submits two memorials in succession. His motive is plain enough."

sentences.zh: 純仁凡薦引人材，必以天下公議，其人不知自純仁所出。

translations.literal: Whenever Chunren recommended men for office, he always relied on public consensus under Heaven; the men themselves did not know the recommendation came from Chunren.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Chunren recommended men for office, he always relied on the consensus of public opinion throughout the realm; the men themselves did not know the recommendation had come from Chunren.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「為宰相，豈可不牢籠天下士，使知出於門下？」

translations.literal: Someone said: "As chancellor, should you not win over the scholars under Heaven so they know they owe their rise to your patronage?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "As chancellor, should you not win over the scholars of the realm so they know they owe their advancement to your patronage?"

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：'但朝廷進用不失正人，何必知出於我邪？」

translations.literal: Chunren said: "So long as the court promotes upright men, why must they know it came from me?"
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "So long as the court promotes upright men, why must they know the appointment came from me?"

sentences.zh: 哲宗既召章惇為相，純仁堅請去，遂以觀文殿大學士加右正議大夫知潁昌府。

translations.literal: After Zhezong recalled Zhang Dun as chancellor, Chunren firmly asked to leave and was made magistrate of Yingchang Prefecture with the titles Grand Academician of the Hall for Exalted Literature and Right Regular Grandee of Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhezong recalled Zhang Dun as chancellor, Chunren firmly asked to leave office and was made magistrate of Yingchang Prefecture with the titles Grand Academician of the Hall for Exalted Literature and Right Regular Grandee of Discussion.

sentences.zh: 入辭，哲宗曰：「卿不肯為朕留，雖在外，于時政有見，宜悉以聞，毋事形跡。」

translations.literal: On taking leave he was told by Zhezong: "Since you will not stay for Us, though you are outside the capital, if you have views on current policy you should report them all—do not stand on ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave, Emperor Zhezong told him, "Since you will not stay for me, though you are outside the capital, if you have views on current policy you should report them fully—do not stand on ceremony."

sentences.zh: 徙河南府，又徙陳州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Henan Prefecture, then again to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Henan Prefecture, then again to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，哲宗嘗言：「貶謫之人，殆似永廢。」

translations.literal: Earlier Zhezong had once said: "Men who are demoted and banished are nearly as good as permanently discarded."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Zhezong had once said, "Men who are demoted and banished are nearly as good as permanently cast aside."

sentences.zh: 純仁前賀曰：「陛下念及此，堯、舜用心也。」

translations.literal: Chunren had congratulated him beforehand: "Your Majesty's concern for this shows the mind of Yao and Shun."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren had congratulated him on this beforehand, saying, "Your Majesty's concern for this shows the mind of Yao and Shun."

sentences.zh: 既而呂大防等竄嶺表，會明堂肆赦，章惇先期言：「此數十人，當終身勿徙。」

translations.literal: Then Lü Dafang and others were banished to Lingnan; when the Hall of Brightness amnesty was proclaimed, Zhang Dun spoke beforehand: "These several dozen men should never be moved for the rest of their lives."
translations.idiomatic: Then Lü Dafang and others were banished to Lingnan. When the Hall of Brightness amnesty was proclaimed, Zhang Dun spoke beforehand, "These several dozen men should never be moved for the rest of their lives."

sentences.zh: 純仁聞而憂憤，欲齋戒上疏申理之。

translations.literal: Chunren, hearing this, was troubled and indignant and wished to fast and submit a memorial in their defense.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren, hearing this, was troubled and indignant and wished to fast and submit a memorial in their defense.

sentences.zh: 所親勸以勿為觸怒，萬一遠斥，非高年所宜。

translations.literal: Those close to him urged him not to provoke anger—for if he were banished far away, that would not suit a man of advanced years.
translations.idiomatic: Those close to him urged him not to provoke anger—for if he were banished far away, that would not suit a man of his advanced years.

sentences.zh: 純仁曰：「事至於此，無一人敢言，若上心遂回，所系大矣。

translations.literal: Chunren said: "Matters have come to this and not one person dares speak. If the emperor's mind should turn back on this, the consequences would be grave.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren said, "Matters have come to this and not one person dares speak. If the emperor's mind should harden on this course, the consequences would be grave.

sentences.zh: 不然，死亦何憾。」

translations.literal: If not, what regret would there be in death?"
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, what regret would there be in death?"

sentences.zh: 乃疏曰：「大防等年老疾病，不習水土，炎荒非久處之地，又憂虞不測，何以自存。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Dafang and the others are old and ill, unused to the climate and soil; the hot wastes are no place to remain long, and with unpredictable dangers besides, how could they preserve themselves?
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Dafang and the others are old and ill, unused to the climate and soil; the hot southern wastes are no place to remain long, and with unpredictable dangers besides, how could they preserve themselves?

sentences.zh: 臣曾與大防等共事，多被排斥，陛下之所親見。

translations.literal: Your subject once served with Dafang and the others and was often pushed aside—Your Majesty saw this yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject once served with Dafang and the others and was often pushed aside—Your Majesty saw this with your own eyes.

sentences.zh: 臣之激切，止是仰報聖德。

translations.literal: Your subject's urgency is only to repay in loyalty the sage virtue of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's urgency is only to repay in loyalty the sage virtue of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 向來章惇、呂惠卿雖為貶謫，不出裏居。

translations.literal: In the past, though Zhang Dun and Lü Huiqing were demoted and banished, they did not leave their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, though Zhang Dun and Lü Huiqing were demoted and banished, they did not leave their home districts.

sentences.zh: 臣向曾有言，深蒙陛下開納，陛下以一蔡確之故，常軫聖念。

translations.literal: Your subject spoke on this before and was deeply received by Your Majesty's open acceptance; Your Majesty, because of Cai Que alone, has often borne this in sage concern.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject spoke on this before and was deeply received by Your Majesty's open acceptance; Your Majesty, because of Cai Que alone, has often borne this in sage concern.

sentences.zh: 今赴彥若已死貶所，將不止一蔡確矣。

translations.literal: Now Fu Yanruo has already died in his place of banishment—there will be more than one Cai Que.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fu Yanruo has already died in his place of banishment—there will be more than one Cai Que.

sentences.zh: 願陛下斷自淵衷，將大防等引赦原放。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, I beg you to decide from the depths of your heart and bring Dafang and the others back under the amnesty and release them."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, I beg you to decide from the depths of your heart and bring Dafang and the others back under the amnesty and release them."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，忤惇意，詆為同罪，落職知隨州。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted it offended Zhang Dun, who denounced him as guilty of the same offense; he was stripped of office and made prefect of Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted it offended Zhang Dun, who denounced him as guilty of the same offense; he was stripped of office and made prefect of Sui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，又貶武安軍節度副使、永州安置。

translations.literal: The next year he was further demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Wu'an Army and settled at Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was further demoted to Vice Commissioner of the Wu'an Army and settled at Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時疾失明，聞命怡然就道。

translations.literal: By then illness had blinded him; on receiving the order he set out calmly on the road.
translations.idiomatic: By then illness had blinded him; on receiving the order he set out calmly on the road.

sentences.zh: 或謂近名，純仁曰：「七十之年，兩目俱喪，萬里之行，豈其欲哉？

translations.literal: Some said he sought reputation; Chunren said: "At seventy, with both eyes gone, on a journey of ten thousand li—could that be what I wanted?
translations.idiomatic: Some said he sought reputation; Chunren said, "At seventy, with both eyes gone, on a journey of ten thousand li—could that be what I wanted?

sentences.zh: 但區區之愛君，有懷不盡，若避好名之嫌，則無為善之路矣。」

translations.literal: It is only my small measure of love for my ruler, with feelings not yet fully expressed. If I shunned the suspicion of seeking a good name, there would be no path left for doing good."
translations.idiomatic: It is only my small measure of love for my ruler, with feelings not yet fully expressed. If I shunned the suspicion of seeking a good name, there would be no path left for doing good."

sentences.zh: 每戒子弟毋得小有不平，聞諸子怨章惇，純仁必怒止之。

translations.literal: He always warned his sons and grandsons not to harbor the least resentment; when he heard his sons resent Zhang Dun, Chunren always angrily stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: He always warned his sons and grandsons not to harbor the least resentment; when he heard his sons speak with resentment of Zhang Dun, Chunren always angrily stopped them.

sentences.zh: 江行赴貶所，舟覆，扶純仁出，衣盡濕。

translations.literal: Traveling by river to his place of banishment, the boat capsized; they pulled Chunren out and his clothes were soaked through.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling by river to his place of banishment, the boat capsized; they pulled Chunren out, and his clothes were soaked through.

sentences.zh: 顧諸子曰：「此豈章惇為之哉？」

translations.literal: He looked at his sons and said: "Surely Zhang Dun did not do this?"
translations.idiomatic: He looked at his sons and said, "Surely Zhang Dun did not do this?"

sentences.zh: 既至永，韓維責均州，其子訴維執政日與司馬光不合，得免行。

translations.literal: When he reached Yong, Han Wei was assigned to Jun Prefecture; his son petitioned that during Wei's time in power he had been at odds with Sima Guang, and Wei was excused from going.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Yong, Han Wei was assigned to Jun Prefecture; Wei's son petitioned that during Wei's time in power he had been at odds with Sima Guang, and Wei was excused from going.

sentences.zh: 純仁之子欲以純仁與光議役法不同為請，純仁曰：「吾用君實薦，以至宰相。

translations.literal: Chunren's sons wished to petition on the ground that Chunren and Guang had differed on the labor-service law; Chunren said: "I reached the chancellorship through Junshi's recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren's sons wished to petition on the ground that Chunren and Sima Guang had differed on the labor-service law; Chunren said, "I reached the chancellorship through Junshi's recommendation.

sentences.zh: 昔同朝論事不合則可，汝輩以為今日之言，則不可也。

translations.literal: In the past, differing in court debate was permissible—but for you to speak as you do today is not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, differing in court debate was permissible—but for you to speak as you do today is not permissible.

sentences.zh: 有愧心而生者，不若無愧心而死。」

translations.literal: Better to die without a guilty conscience than to live with one."
translations.idiomatic: Better to die without a guilty conscience than to live with one."

sentences.zh: 其子乃止。

translations.literal: His sons then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His sons then stopped.

sentences.zh: 居三年，徽宗即位，欽聖顯肅後同聽政，即日授純仁光祿卿，分司南京，鄧州居住。

translations.literal: After three years Emperor Huizong ascended the throne; Empress Qinsheng Xiansu joined in governance and that same day appointed Chunren Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with nominal office at Nanjing and residence at Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After three years Emperor Huizong ascended the throne; Empress Qinsheng Xiansu joined in governance and that same day appointed Chunren Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with nominal office at Nanjing and residence at Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 遣中使至永賜茶藥，諭曰：「皇帝在藩邸，太皇太后在宮中，知公先朝言事忠直，今虛相位以待，不知目疾如何，用何人醫之。」

translations.literal: An imperial envoy was sent to Yong with tea and medicine and instructed him: "When the emperor was still in his princely residence and the Grand Empress Dowager was in the palace, they knew of your loyal and upright remonstrance in the previous reign. Now the chancellorship waits empty for you—we do not know how your eye ailment is, or what physician should treat it."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy was sent to Yong with tea and medicine and instructed him, "When the emperor was still in his princely residence and the Grand Empress Dowager was in the palace, they knew of your loyal and upright remonstrance in the previous reign. Now the chancellorship waits empty for you—we do not know how your eye ailment is, or what physician should treat it."

sentences.zh: 純仁頓首謝。

translations.literal: Chunren bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren bowed his head in thanks.

sentences.zh: 道除右正議大夫、提舉崇福宮。

translations.literal: On the road he was appointed Right Regular Grandee of Discussion and Director of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he was appointed Right Regular Grandee of Discussion and Director of Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 不數月，以觀文殿大學士、中太一宮使詔之。

translations.literal: Within a few months he was summoned with the titles Grand Academician of the Hall for Exalted Literature and Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he was summoned with the titles Grand Academician of the Hall for Exalted Literature and Commissioner of the Central Grand Unity Palace.

sentences.zh: 有曰：「豈唯尊德尚齒，昭示寵優；

translations.literal: It read: "Surely this honors virtue and reveres age and displays special favor;
translations.idiomatic: The edict read, "Surely this honors virtue and reveres age and displays special favor;

sentences.zh: 庶幾鯁論嘉謀，日聞忠告。」

translations.literal: perhaps forthright counsel and good plans may daily reach the ear as loyal admonition."
translations.idiomatic: perhaps forthright counsel and good plans may daily reach the ear as loyal admonition."

sentences.zh: 純仁以疾，捧詔而泣曰：「上果用我矣，死有餘責。」

translations.literal: Chunren, ill, received the edict weeping and said: "The emperor truly intends to use me—death would still leave duty unfulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Chunren, ill, received the edict weeping and said, "The emperor truly intends to use me—even in death there would still be duty unfulfilled."

sentences.zh: 徽宗又遣中使賜茶藥，促入覲，仍宣渴見之意。

translations.literal: Huizong again sent an imperial envoy with tea and medicine, urging him to come for audience and conveying the emperor's eager wish to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huizong again sent an imperial envoy with tea and medicine, urging him to come for audience and conveying the emperor's eager wish to see him.

sentences.zh: 純仁乞歸許養疾，徽宗不得已許之。

translations.literal: Chunren begged to return home to nurse his illness; Huizong unwillingly granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren begged to return home to nurse his illness; Emperor Huizong, unwillingly, granted it.

sentences.zh: 每見輔臣問安否，乃曰：「范純仁，得一識面足矣。」

translations.literal: Whenever he saw chief ministers he asked after Chunren's health and would say: "Fan Chunren—one meeting would be enough."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw chief ministers he asked after Chunren's health and would say, "Fan Chunren—even one meeting would be enough."

sentences.zh: 遂遣上醫視疾。

translations.literal: He then sent the court physician to examine his illness.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent the court physician to examine his illness.

sentences.zh: 疾小愈，丐以所得冠帔改服色酬醫。

translations.literal: When his illness eased slightly, he asked to exchange the rank robes he had received for official robes in payment to the physician.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness eased slightly, he asked to exchange the rank robes he had received for official robes in payment to the physician.

sentences.zh: 詔賜醫章服，令以冠帔與族侄。

translations.literal: An edict granted the physician official robes and ordered the rank robes given to a clan nephew.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the physician official robes and ordered the rank robes given to a clan nephew.

sentences.zh: 疾革，以宣仁後誣謗未明為恨。

translations.literal: When his illness became critical, he regretted that the slander against Empress Xuanren had not been cleared.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness became critical, he regretted that the slander against Empress Dowager Xuanren had not been cleared.

sentences.zh: 呼諸子口占遺表，命門生李之儀次第之。

translations.literal: He called his sons and dictated a final memorial, ordering his disciple Li Zhiyi to put it in order.
translations.idiomatic: He called his sons and dictated a final memorial, ordering his disciple Li Zhiyi to put it in order.

sentences.zh: 其略云：「蓋嘗先天下而憂，期不負聖人之學，此先臣所以教子，而微臣資以事君。」

translations.literal: Its gist read: "I have always sought to worry before all under Heaven and hoped not to fail the learning of the sages—this is what my late father taught his sons, and what your humble servant relied on in serving his ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Its gist read, "I have always sought to worry before all under Heaven and hoped not to fail the learning of the sages—this is what my late father taught his sons, and what your humble servant relied on in serving his ruler."

sentences.zh: 又云：「惟宣仁之誣謗未明，致保佑之憂勤不顯。」

translations.literal: It also read: "Only because the slander against Xuanren has not been cleared do the protective labors and earnest care remain unrevealed."
translations.idiomatic: It also read, "Only because the slander against Empress Dowager Xuanren has not been cleared do her protective labors and earnest care remain unrevealed."

sentences.zh: 又云：「未解疆埸之嚴，幾空帑藏之積。

translations.literal: It also read: "The frontier defenses were not yet secure, and the treasury's accumulations were nearly emptied.
translations.idiomatic: It also read, "The frontier defenses were not yet secure, and the treasury's accumulations were nearly emptied.

sentences.zh: 有城必守，得地難耕。」

translations.literal: Where there was a fort it had to be held; land taken was hard to farm."
translations.idiomatic: Where there was a fort it had to be held; land taken was hard to farm."

sentences.zh: 凡八事。

translations.literal: There were eight items in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were eight items in all.

sentences.zh: 建中靖國改元之旦，受家人賀。

translations.literal: On the first day of the Jianzhong Jingguo era change he received congratulations from his family.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the Jianzhong Jingguo era change he received congratulations from his family.

sentences.zh: 明日，熟寐而卒。

translations.literal: The next day he fell into a deep sleep and died.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he fell into a deep sleep and died.

sentences.zh: 年七十五。

translations.literal: He was seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 詔賻白金三十兩，敕許、洛官給其葬，贈開府儀同三司，諡曰忠宣，禦書碑額曰：「世濟忠直之碑」。

translations.literal: An edict granted thirty taels of white silver for funeral expenses; Xu and Lu officials were ordered to supply the burial; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with equal ceremonial to the Three Excellencies; his posthumous title was Zhongxuan; the imperial brush inscribed the stele: "Stele of Loyalty and Uprightness Handed Down through Generations."
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted thirty taels of white silver for funeral expenses; officials of Xu and Lu were ordered to supply the burial; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with ceremonial equal to the Three Excellencies; his posthumous title was Zhongxuan; the imperial brush inscribed the stele: "Stele of Loyalty and Uprightness Handed Down through Generations."

sentences.zh: 純仁性夷易寬簡，不以聲色加人，誼之所在，則挺然不少屈。

translations.literal: Chunren's nature was easy, broad, and simple; he did not use harsh tone or appearance toward others, yet where righteousness lay he stood firm and would not yield in the least.
translations.idiomatic: Chunren's nature was easy, broad, and simple; he did not use harsh tone or appearance toward others, yet where righteousness lay he stood firm and would not yield in the least.

sentences.zh: 自為布衣至宰相，廉儉如一，所得奉賜，皆以廣義莊；

translations.literal: From commoner to chancellor he was frugal and plain in the same way; all salary and gifts he received he used for the Broad Righteousness Estate;
translations.idiomatic: From commoner to chancellor he was frugal and plain in the same way; all salary and gifts he received he used for the Broad Righteousness Estate;

sentences.zh: 前後任子恩，多先疏族。

translations.literal: whenever he used the privilege of office for his sons, he mostly gave priority to distant clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: whenever he used the privilege of office for his sons, he mostly gave priority to distant clansmen.

sentences.zh: 沒之日，幼子、五孫猶未官。

translations.literal: On the day he died, his youngest son and five grandsons still held no office.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, his youngest son and five grandsons still held no office.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾平生所學，得之忠恕二字，一生用不盡。

translations.literal: He once said: "What I have learned in life I owe to the two words loyalty and forbearance—a lifetime is not enough to exhaust them.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "What I have learned in life I owe to the two words loyalty and forbearance—a lifetime is not enough to exhaust them.

sentences.zh: 以至立朝事君，接待僚友，親睦宗族，未嘗須臾離此也。」

translations.literal: Whether standing in court serving the ruler, receiving colleagues, or treating kin with kindness in the clan, I have never for a moment departed from this."
translations.idiomatic: Whether standing in court serving the ruler, receiving colleagues, or treating kin with kindness in the clan, I have never for a moment departed from this."

sentences.zh: 每戒子弟曰：「人雖至愚，責人則明；

translations.literal: He always warned his sons and grandsons: "However foolish a man may be, in blaming others he is clear;
translations.idiomatic: He always warned his sons and grandsons, "However foolish a man may be, in blaming others he is clear;

sentences.zh: 雖有聰明，恕己則昏。

translations.literal: however clever he may be, in forgiving himself he is dull.
translations.idiomatic: however clever he may be, in forgiving himself he is dull.

sentences.zh: 苟能以責人之心責己，恕己之心恕人，不患不至聖賢地位也。」

translations.literal: If one can blame oneself with the mind one uses to blame others, and forgive others with the mind one uses to forgive oneself, one need not fear failing to reach the station of sages."
